Sainsbury’s has agreed to sell its Argos business to Swift Partners in a deal worth at least £120 million.

The UK’s second-largest supermarket chain said the firm will buy Argos standalone stores, as well as its stores within Sainsbury’s shops, on a long-term agreement, including its logistics network, pet insurance and product warranty cover.

Swift will also buy Sainsbury’s distribution centre in Daventry and Sainsbury’s sourcing offices located in Shanghai and Hong Kong as part of the deal.

Swift is a new firm set up by retail experts including former Co-operative Group boss Richard Pennycook, former Morrisons chief operating officer Trevor Strain, and backed by Matt Truman and his retail investment and advisory firm, True Capital.

Sainsbury’s will get cash proceeds of at least £120 million from the sale, with a £70 million up-front payment when the deal completes, which is expected in February next year.

open image in gallery Supermarket Sainsbury’s has agreed to sell its Argos business to Swift Partners ( PA )

Last month, the retailer said recent trading has been “encouraging” despite continued uncertainty over the impact of the Middle East conflict on its shoppers.

The chain was buoyed by stronger growth in its core grocery business, while general merchandise – which includes clothing brand Tu – and its Argos business both reported declines.

It revealed that total retail sales, excluding fuel, grew by 2.7 per cent to £9.15 billion in the 16 weeks to June 20, compared with the same period a year earlier.

Sales of the Sainsbury’s brand grew 3.1 per cent to £8.04 billion over the quarter, with grocery sales up 3.6 per cent year on year.

Bosses suggested the firm had recorded growth supported by investment into value, such as through its Aldi price match and Nectar price discounts.

Nevertheless, grocery growth was partly offset by a 3.7 per cent sales fall in its general merchandise and clothing business.

The group said sales at its Argos business dipped 0.5 per cent as positive volume growth was “offset by the impact of subdued consumer spending on average selling price”.

Chief executive Simon Roberts said: “Customers are looking for value now more than ever. We are consistently delivering outstanding quality at great value, so more people are choosing Sainsbury’s for their big weekly shop.

“This has driven an encouraging start to the year with continued volume growth and market outperformance.

“With the World Cup in full swing and an exciting summer of sport ahead, I want to say a huge thank you to all our Sainsbury’s and Argos colleagues and our farmers and suppliers for showing up so well for our customers every day.”

Thousands of migrants streamed into the Moroccan town of Fnideq near the border with Ceuta overnight, despite a deployment of security that foiled most attempts to cross into the Spanish enclave.

Spanish Interior Ministry said 18 people died on Thursday trying to enter Ceuta in North Africa, as migrants rushed by sea and ⁠land from Morocco.

Local media report between ​2,000 ⁠and 3,000 people crossed ‌into Ceuta on Thursday.

Spain sent military and police reinforcements to Ceuta on Thursday after the surge.

open image in gallery Soldiers patrol near the Spanish-Moroccan border in Ceuta, Spain, July 31, 2026. REUTERS/Fabian Bimmer ( Reuters )

Ceuta, along with Melilla, another Spanish autonomous ‌city in northern Morocco, represents ​the European Union's ‌only land border ⁠with Africa. Both cities ⁠periodically experience surges in attempted crossings ‌by migrants ​seeking to ‌reach Europe.

Spanish state television TVE ⁠said between 2,000 and 3,000 people crossed into Ceuta on Thursday. Most of those who succeeded in crossing appeared to have done so before midday, according to residents of Fnideq.

Where is Ceuta?

Spain sent military ​and ⁠police reinforcements to Ceuta after the surge, while authorities in the enclave said nine bodies had been retrieved.

Although the border crossing appeared blocked, groups of migrants moved along the coast seeking ⁠routes around the fence and some prepared to swim. "I was late," said Brahim, 32, who gave ​only one ⁠name. He said he had arrived from ‌Tangier hoping to cross through the gate but found it effectively shut.

Among those hoping to cross into the enclave of 85,000 were women and children as well from Morocco and Sub-Saharan Africa.

Moroccan authorities deployed ‌water cannon trucks and reinforced security at the crossing-gates, repeatedly pushing back ‌migrants attempting to approach.

open image in gallery Migrants from Morocco react as they crossed into Ceuta by sea, at the border between the Spanish enclave of Ceuta and Morocco, as seen from Ceuta, Spain, July 30, 2026 ( Reuters )

Nearby stood the charred remains of a bus and seven vehicles, left after clashes that erupted as authorities sought to stop the crowds, according to Reuters witnesses.

Another migrant said he had been caught in a stampede ⁠during an attempted crossing.

"I feared for my life," said the migrant, who declined to give his name, as he described chaotic scenes of people pushing and stepping on one another along a narrow coastal route.

Traffic clogged roads into Fnideq as would-be migrants, including minors, continued to arrive. Some trudged along the highway into the city late into the night, while others took mountain paths to avoid checkpoints.

open image in gallery Vehicles burn in Fnideq, Morocco, July 31, 2026, as migrants (not pictured) wait for a chance to cross to the Spanish enclave of Ceuta. Picture taken with a mobile phone. REUTERS/Ahmed El Jechtimi ( Reuters )

Security forces repeatedly turned back people making concerted rushes on the crossing through the night hours, while migrants regrouped on roads, hills and ‌open spaces across the city.

Spain's Socialist government stands out in Europe for its pro-migrant stance, and ​has recently launched a programme to provide legal status for some 500,000 undocumented migrants, triggering an ‌influx of applications double that number.

Early on ⁠Friday, Fatima Mahli, 23, sat with her two daughters on a patch of grass beside the ⁠road to the crossing.

The resident of Morocco's northern city of Tetouan said her husband had left before dawn to try to ‌swim to Ceuta.

"I thought I ​could cross by foot through the border. But ‌we are stuck here, unable to go back home," ​she said.

"I was hoping to cross as a family but my husband woke up early and went first, swimming."

TV presenter and Newcastle United fan Declan Donnelly has paid an emotional tribute to his "childhood hero" Kevin Keegan following the football legend's death aged 75.

Keegan, a revered figure who managed Newcastle United and also played for the club for two years, passed away on 20 July after a battle with stage four cancer.

Donnelly, alongside his presenting partner Anthony McPartlin, honoured Keegan on their podcast, Hanging Out With Ant And Dec.

The duo hailed him as a "true legend to Newcastle United supporters," reflecting on his profound impact.

They opened the episode by acknowledging Keegan's immense significance to the people of the North East.

Ant and Dec with Kevin Keegan in 1995 ( Getty )

“Kevin Keegan was the reason that I really got into football, he was the David Beckham of his day. He was the Lionel Messi and the Cristiano Ronaldo of the 70s and 80s,” Donnelly said.

The 50-year-old continued: “He signed for Newcastle United in 1982, which is when my eldest brother had started taking me to football.

“Him signing for Newcastle was huge news, and that started my rollercoaster love affair with Newcastle United and football.

“He was my childhood hero. When we got the news through last week, I was absolutely devastated.

“I’m not ashamed to say I shed a tear.”

Donnelly, who is from Newcastle upon Tyne, added: “He just meant so much to the people of the North East.

“What he gave to us in his energy and enthusiasm and the hope he gave us for our football team.

“He just meant so much beyond football to the whole region. He was just such a special man.

“We were lucky enough to meet him on a couple of occasions.”

Donnelly, known for hosting shows such as I’m A Celebrity… Get Me Out Of Here, also recalled meeting Keegan for the first time when he was a young boy after he won a competition.

He grew visibly emotional and said: “That was the best. They say you should never meet heroes, but he was absolutely the exception.”

“I shed a tear last week, and I shed another one this morning,” Donnelly added.

McPartlin also shared his sentiments about the football star, nicknamed “King Kev”, and said: “Words like legends and saviours get bandied around, but he did – he saved our club when he came back as manager.

“He’s a true legend of the game, and to Newcastle United supporters, and he will be missed.”

For almost 50 years Nick Rhodes has been the charismatic and groundbreaking dandy in Duran Duran.

With the blond hair and eye make-up of the 1980s New Romantic he wears to this day he stood out long before the style became fashionable. And not just because of his androgynous appearance.

Rhodes not only pioneered the use of synthesisers to compose classic pop anthems, but also the art of creating spectacular videos to showcase them.

Duran Duran have sold 100 million records since forming in Birmingham half a century ago – and are still selling out concert halls today on their current tour of the UK and Europe.

Rhodes, the only ever present member of the band, took time out from the tour to take part in a candid and wide-ranging Independent TV interview with Geordie Greig, editor in chief of The Independent.

In it, Rhodes reveals that Duran Duran would have split up years ago if not for a timely intervention by another rock ‘n roll great survivor, Mick Jagger.

Watch The Talk Show: Geordie Greig’s interview with Nick Rhodes in full below

He talks about “hanging out” with “dear friend” and role model David Bowie; the day he realised singer Simon Le Bon’s star quality and why he does not take drugs (“I can never slow down so the last thing I wanted was a pile of drugs!”).

He discloses why he still dyes his hair blond (“people underestimate blonds”); why he still wears eye liner (“stick a bit on and it hides it all!”) and why he never wears jeans (“they’re just laziness”.)

And he reveals the secret that explains Duran Duran’s famously visual songs (“songs to me are like paintings”).

open image in gallery The Independent's editor-in-chief Geordie Greig with Duran Duran's Nick Rhodes ( Independent TV )

Most bizarre of all, Rhodes explains why one of his most prized possessions is a collection of cheese labels.

In black trousers and silken jacket he glides across the hallway of the Cafe Royale, before heading to the penthouse Dome suite for his mid-tour interview.

There were a couple of periods when Duran Duran risked splitting and going their separate ways, but Jagger’s advice to Rhodes in the mid-Eighties was crucial.

“Mick looked at me and said ‘You know you really do need to stick together, that is your future.’ He was right because it could all have fallen apart at that time.”

open image in gallery Duran Duran pose at Heathrow Airport before departing for Australia, July 1983. L-R: Bassists John and Andy Taylor (unrelated), singer Simon Le Bon, drummer Roger Taylor and keyboardist Nick Rhodes ( Getty )

Not only making sure the band stayed together he also veered away from the most destructive ingredient in rock n roll: drugs, though not before seeing the havoc it can wreak. He says his hyperactive creative mind was an asset.

“It (drugs) never appealed to me much. My mind moved too quickly anyway. I can never slow down so the last thing I wanted was a pile of drugs. I tried some and it didn’t suit me. I am also somewhat of a control freak so the idea of taking something when you don’t know what is going to happen is thoroughly unappealing. I have been around plenty of it and seen the effects.”

The band was thrown into a world where huge music stars went from being heroes (David Bowie posters were on his childhood bedroom wall) to becoming friends. “By the time I saw David Bowie I no longer wanted to be an astronaut or a magician, two early desires. I wanted to be a musician.”

open image in gallery New Romantic: Nick Rhodes in 1983 ( Getty Images )

Rhodes not only changed his surname from Bates, also his hair colour and his career trajectory. “David was a dear friend, an intellectual - and funny as hell. I liked him very much because he wasn't a let down.”

Initially his parents, both from Birmingham wanted him to be doctor or lawyer - not a rock n roll star - and reluctantly allowed him to take a year off from school at 16 to pursue his music dream. He recalls his mother telling him: “All right darling, you’ve got a year.” They ended up giving him two years – by which time he was on the road to stardom.

It was a journey which he always foresaw for himself with a restless confidence: he was desperate to see the world, never be bored, spurred by aesthetics, imagination and music.

When Rhodes met Warhol in the US, Duran Duran were still just another obscure British band trying to emulate The Beatles and “break” America. Warhol adored the unisexual look of the awestruck Midlands youngsters, chronicling his infatuation in his diaries.

Rhodes says: “We were young kids from Birmingham in New York - and the next minute we were in ‘Andy’s Factory’.”

Princess Diana was another celebrity Duran Duran admirer. She owned their LPs and copies signed by her in a schoolgirl scrawl sold at auction ended up being given to her two boys, William and Harry. “We met her several times,” says Rhodes. “She was a great fan to have. I used to see her around in Chelsea.”

Guided by his love of aesthetics, Rhodes strove to pursue good taste and fine detail both in his songs and his style, traits reflected by influences such as Bryan Ferry and Bowie.

He still goes to great trouble over his style. For instance, he never, ever, wears blue jeans: “To me jeans are just laziness. I don’t like the cut.”

open image in gallery No blue jeans:L Nick Rhodes and Alexandra Stama at The Serpentine Gallery Summer Party, 2023 ( Getty )

Nor has being well into his sixties stopped him wearing his trademark black eye-liner. He enjoys the 10 minutes it takes him to do it each day: “I like the routine of it. I can look in the mirror and go “he looks a bit tired.”’ He jokes: “Stick a bit of eye liner on and you can hide it all!”

Former art student Rhodes’ artistic talent extends well beyond music, fashion and film to photography and pop art, which is why he has published a book of abstract art, called Interference, which was the subject of an exhibition in London - and his photographs have been published in magazines such as Tatler.

Rhodes, now 64, was married for eight years to Julie Anne Friedman, whom, appropriately for a band whose most famous music video, “Rio”, was filmed on a yacht, he met at a yacht party. The couple had a daughter, now in her 30s. Rhodes has had a series of relationships with women since then but has not remarried.

Occasionally, Rhodes guiding star and relentless pursuit of art and beauty gives way to old fashioned English eccentricity.

Such as one of his proudest possessions, a large collection of cheese labels. He inherited it from his dad. Rhodes laughs: “He’d even done them by the weight of the cheese snd the colours - there was something about it that was rather fabulous.”

Rhodes has surfed the rock world for half a century as one the first, and in the eyes of some the greatest, practitioner of the synthesiser.

open image in gallery Duran Duran's singer Simon Le Bon and Rhodes perform during the opening ceremony for the Commonwealth Games at the Alexander Stadium in Birmingham, 2022 ( AFP/Getty )

He says: “I treat it as I might treat an orchestra. I can play any instruments (on it)… like a flute or a big bass drum or a violin. I can make textures and I build up an arrangement within the songs…”

It is part of the special alchemy of Duran Duran that Rhodes embodies their musical and fashion style, sitting silent and partly concealed behind his synth keyboard during gigs, while dynamic lead singer and “frontman” Simon Le Bon is its more visible official face.

Rhodes recalls the moment he first heard Le Bon sing: “We'd been through several vocalists. But when he walked in and sung a note, I thought, ‘That's it. He’s the one.’” It was obvious Le Bon was like Jagger, Bowie and Freddie Mercury, says Rhodes, “unique and distinctive – Simon had that.”

Rhodes is the official keeper of the vast wardrobe of exotic clothes the band have worn over the years. He would love to see it feature in a V&A exhibition along the lines of the museum’s successful show featuring the man who inspired him, Bowie.

Rhodes – and Duran Duran – deserve it.

British Airways’ parent company International Airlines Group (IAG) has revealed a 35% slump in profits because of soaring fuel costs.

The group reported pre-tax profits tumbling to 732 million euro (£627 million) in the three months to the end of June, from 1.1 billion euro (£940 million) a year earlier.

The company’s fuel costs and emissions charges rose by 23%, linked to the conflict in the Middle East.

IAG">

Its revenue was stable at 8,883 million euro (£7,603 million).

IAG chief executive Luis Gallego insisted the group has “excellent fundamentals”, and its diverse portfolio of brands means it is well positioned to deal with “near-term headwinds”.

The company, which also owns the Iberia, Vueling and Level airlines, said it expects demand for travel across its network to “remain strong”.

About 57% of its seats have been booked for the second half of the year, with revenue from those bookings in line with last year.

It added that it expects its long-haul markets to “remain positive” and short-haul flights to be “competitive”.

open image in gallery The company also owns the Iberia, Vueling and Level airlines (PA) ( PA Archive )

IAG’s pre-tax profits for the six months to June 30 were down 21%, from 1.3 billion euro (£1.1 billion) to 1.0 billion euro (£850 million).

Its revenue over this period rose by 1% to 16.1 billion euro (£13.8 billion).

Some 57.9 million passengers flew on the company’s flights in the first half of the year, which was relatively flat compared with 2025.

Mr Gallego said: “With these results IAG has again demonstrated that its excellent fundamentals are supporting continued value creation for our shareholders, despite the impact of the crisis in the Middle East and wider geopolitical events.

“We are well-positioned to deal with these near-term headwinds with a diverse portfolio of world-class brands in large and attractive markets; industry-leading margins; significant free cash flow and a strong balance sheet; and attractive shareholder returns.

“Our long-term transformation programme has created the resilience that we are now benefiting from – products and services that our customers value, efficient and punctual operations and a low cost base.”

He added: “We remain confident in our business model and strategy that has made us one of the best-performing airline groups in the world.”

News.title: What does under the gun mean in poker?
News.content:
Poker remains one of the most popular card games on the planet, though it can often appear complicated to those who aren’t in the know, or inexperienced players.

One particularly vital part of poker that contains plenty of special terms and acronyms is the table positioning.

Put simply, understanding poker table positions is important for making strategic decisions, though you need to get up to speed with the different positions and how they might shape a strategy first.

And one of the most important positions is known as “under the gun”. Also referred to as ‘UTG’, this is a particularly critical position in Texas Hold’em as the player seated immediately to the left of the big blind.

This article will break down what under the gun means, its challenges, and how players can adapt their UTG poker strategy when in position on the best online poker sites.

What does under the gun mean in poker?

Under the gun (UTG) is used to describe the player who is first to act in the pre-flop betting round. They are seated immediately to the left of the big blind, so they are the third position to the left of the dealer.

Playing under the gun poker is one of the most challenging positions in Texas Hold’em, because you have no information on other players’ actions. You are the third to act after the flop, so though you do have a positional advantage on the small blind and big blind, you are still at a disadvantage positionally compared to three – or six – other players.

Being UTG affects decision-making and the need for tight play. Most advice would suggest that whoever is UTG should play tighter, and make sure to only play on a better range of hands. Folding is a useful strategy for players who are sitting in this position too.

How to play from under the gun

Playing carefully from under the gun can prevent losing chips early in the hand, so we have offered some practical tips for playing in this position.

Play fewer hands: Due to the limited information that is available to those sitting at UTG, it is advisable to play a tight aggressive game. Make sure to only play hands that you are very confident are strong – overall, this will lead to playing fewer hands than you usually would in other positions.

Focus on premium hands: Make sure you only play hands that you know are strong (for example, pocket Aces, Kings or Queens) in order to avoid getting caught in tricky situations post-flop.

Avoid bluffing too much: When at UTG, don’t bluff too often, as other players can act after you and re-raise. Use bluffing only as part of a tight-aggressive strategy, and once you have established yourself in-game.

Why under the gun is important in Texas Hold’em

Despite potentially being viewed as one of the ‘weaker’ positions at the table, being under the gun in Texas Hold’em is still strategically significant, as this player bets before any other player.

Though their decision will of course be influenced by the cards they are dealt, the actions made in this early position can set the tone for the hand.

Skilled players will often try to exploit this position, so a strong understanding of UTG can give players a competitive edge.

Other poker positions

Below, we’ve provided a brief one-line explanation of each of the other poker table positions in Texas Hold’em.

The button: This is regarded as the best of all the Texas Hold’em positions, as you have the most information when it comes to your turn. Therefore, they have the widest range available to them on each hand.

Small blind: This is the first player to act after the flop, and they usually have the lowest range available to them. They are also forced to bet ‘blind’ (without seeing their cards), which is a significant disadvantage.

Big blind: This is seen as the worst position at the table, as the player is the second player to act on each street after the flop and they also have to bet before seeing their cards.

Under the gun: In a nine-player game, the table can also have under the gun +1 and under the gun +2. These sit one left of the UTG player, and have to use a similarly tight-aggressive strategy.

Lojack: In a nine-player game, the Lojack is essentially the same as the UTG would be in a six-player game. The range of hands you can play is still relatively tight, but you can afford to play looser than the players before you.

Hijack: The Hijack, or HJ, is the second of the so-called ‘middle positions’ at the table. These players can afford to play looser; for example, by adding more off-suit hands with blockers.

The cutoff: The cutoff, or CO, is the penultimate position in the table after the flop. Players sat here can start stealing blinds more aggressively, and if they can make the button fold, then they will be in position for the rest of the round.

Under the gun summary

In summary, as with every position at the table, it is vital to understand the under the gun position, and how to play it effectively.

Playing poker under the gun is often seen as a disadvantage, but it can be a strategically significant position and you can affect other players if you play skilfully.

When playing under the gun poker, remember that being cautious and selective from this position is crucial for long-term success in Texas Hold’em.

Play fewer hands, focus on premium hands and avoid bluffing too much.

News.title: UK economy to flatline, warns Bank of England
News.content:
Britain’s economy is set to almost grind to a halt for the rest of the year, the Bank of England has warned.

Growth will drop to just 0.1pc per quarter, the Bank predicted, slowing sharply after a strong start to 2026.

Higher petrol prices and energy bills, a weak jobs market and rising mortgage costs are all draining confidence and spending power from the economy.

Inflation, which slowed to a 15-month low of 2.6pc in June, is also expected to rise again to 3.2pc later this year, the Bank warned.

Andrew Bailey, the Bank’s Governor, said inflation had “fallen faster than we’d expected” but warned that war in the Middle East would lead to a fresh spike.

He added that growth would “weaken slightly further in the near term as the effects of the conflict weigh further on demand”.

The Bank also predicted that unemployment will rise back above 5pc in the coming months, limiting workers’ ability to ask for higher wages to cope with rising living costs.

It presents a challenging backdrop for Andy Burnham and his Chancellor, John Healey, who have pledged to help voters struggling with the cost of living.

The forecasts came as policymakers led by Mr Bailey held interest rates at 3.75pc.

Although three members of the nine-strong Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) voted for higher rates, up from two at the previous meeting, the Governor dismissed suggestions the Bank is moving towards higher interest rates.

The public should “not… [think] the Bank of England is edging towards a hike,” Mr Bailey said.

“Frankly there is nothing I have said, or any of us have said, along those lines. We took a decision today to leave the Bank Rate unchanged and that is the relevant conclusion.”

Clare Lombardelli, a Deputy Governor, said voting to keep rates at 3.75pc “was not a close judgement”, calling the decision “pretty clear” given slowing inflation in the domestic economy.

Officials are monitoring the economy for any signs that increases in oil, gas and petrol prices caused by the war in Iran are creeping into higher costs and wages in the wider economy.

Mr Bailey said: “The possibility of repeated resumptions of conflict, combined with lower than usual European gas stock levels and a fall in global refining output, mean that risks to energy prices lie to the upside.”

He added: “Reassuringly, there are few signs so far that second-round effects are generating more broad-based inflationary pressures.”

Companies are struggling to pass higher costs on to their customers because of the economy’s weakness, he added.

Workers are typically securing only modest pay rises as the weak jobs market leaves them in a poor position to push for bigger salaries.

Mr Bailey stressed there are still major risks to the outlook given the war and promised to “monitor the situation carefully” and was “ready to adjust our stance”.

“It is our job to ensure that inflation gets back to the 2pc target and stays there, and that is what we will do,” he said.

Borrowing costs dropped in financial markets after the decision.

The Government’s two-year borrowing cost fell from 4.44pc to 4.34pc, the sharpest fall in a month.

The FTSE 250 index of mid-sized UK companies rose 0.8pc to a record high of 24,184.10.

Traders still believe the Bank will raise interest rates twice within a year.

However, Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said rate rises “remain more a threat than a reality”.

He said there was evidence of disinflation in the economy and interest rates could be “cut to 3pc in 2027”, adding: “That’s very different to market pricing for rates to be close to 4.5pc in 2027.”

News.title: Arsonists torch more Ebola clinics as misinformation spirals in DRC
News.content:
Two more Ebola treatment facilities have reportedly been burned down in recent days as health officials struggle to overcome violent public mistrust of medical teams.

At least a dozen facilities have now been attacked since Congo declared its Ebola outbreak amid fear, misinformation and suspicion of outside authorities.

The outbreak is the fastest growing on record and officials said the virus had now killed more than 1,500 people.

The official death toll from the outbreak centred on the north eastern Ituri province of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has risen by 500 in only a week.

Sources told the Telegraph the large jump in deaths was largely caused by a “data harmonisation exercise” between different regions, and the new deaths may not have all happened in the past week.

However, the daily confirmed toll has also continued to climb sharply with the latest government update reporting 50 people dying in the previous 24 hours.

Airfinity, a health analytics firm, said the outbreak “continues to outpace detection and the response” and there is a high chance of it spreading further inside DRC.

News.title: Race for vaccine against new Ebola strain gets $8.5m boost
News.content:
The “most promising” vaccine to tackle the Ebola strain behind an explosive outbreak in the Congo has been given an $8.5 million boost, as researchers race to develop an effective shot.

So far at least 3,360 people have been infected and 1,487 people have died in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), in an epidemic triggered by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola.

But unlike past outbreaks of the more common Zaire strain, there are currently no approved vaccines to tackle Bundibugyo.

On Thursday, the Coalition of Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (Cepi) revealed up to $8.5 million of funding for the only single-dose inoculation, which was described as the “most promising vaccine candidate” by the World Health Organization (WHO) in an analysis in May.

It is being developed by researchers at Hilleman Laboratories – a unique partnership between the pharmaceutical giant Merck and the British philanthropic powerhouse Wellcome, which is headquartered in Singapore.

The vaccine candidate is a Bundibugyo version of the Ervebo shot, which was created by Merck (MSD in Europe) and has already been approved for Ebola Zaire.

It uses a rVSV platform, where a modified version of VSV virus is used to train the immune system to react to target pathogens – in this instance, the Bundibugyo species replaces Zaire.

News.title: AMR chatbot could prevent drug-resistant infections in African hospitals
News.content:
A phone-based chatbot advising medics how to prescribe antibiotics has helped raise the quality of care in African hospitals and should stop bugs developing dangerous resistance, developers say.

Staff at four hospitals across Zambia and Kenya have been using two digital tools in a pilot project to try to address one of the world’s biggest health threats.

Anti-microbial resistance (AMR) is caused by germs evolving so that medicines such as antibiotics designed to kill them no longer work.

The menace is linked to nearly five million deaths each year and makes it increasingly difficult to treat infections. The annual death toll could nearly double in the next 25 years, according to some forecasts.

The rise in AMR is being significantly driven by the misuse and overuse of antimicrobials in human medicine and in agriculture.

Using antibiotics when they are not necessary, using the wrong ones, or getting the dosage wrong, all add to the chances that bugs will develop resistance.

With a shortage of new drugs in the development pipeline, one push to defeat AMR has been to get medics to stick to existing prescription, dosage and treatment advice.

The Antibiotic Stewardship Programme through Innovation, Research, and Education (ASPIRE) is trying to give them guidance using technology they already have in their pockets.

News.title: Tottenham new boys score in shoot-out win over Sydney FC
News.content:
Tonali was brought on as a half-time substitute, before Robertson took the captain’s armband from Archie Gray after he was introduced in the 65th minute.

The former Liverpool left-back delivered three dangerous crosses which went unconverted, something of a theme for a Spurs team who failed to make the most of long spells of dominance.

James Maddison and Mateus Fernandes were not in the match-day squad, while Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven and Jean Paul van Hecke have yet to join the group after the World Cup.

There was another impressive showing from 17-year-old prospect Luca Williams-Barnett, who is pushing for first-team opportunities this upcoming season.

Penalties followed the final whistle, with Spurs scoring all four of their spot kicks. Goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, signed on a free transfer this summer, saved one and Sydney FC’s Josh Lacey hit the post to give Spurs the spoils 4-2.

News.title: Recovery aids and building muscle: Welsh weightlifter Laura Hughes answers your questions
News.content:
Laura Hughes first discovered weightlifting while training at her local Crossfit gym, making the transition from amateur gym-goer to competitive lifting.

Now a member of the Welsh national weightlifting squad, the 33-year-old holds the Welsh record for both the snatch and the clean and jerk (the two official competitive lifts in weightlifting) and is currently third overall in the women’s Welsh rankings. Hughes won bronze at this year’s Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, following on from her third place at the 2018 Games in Australia.

We caught up with her for our Readers Ask series, where industry specialists answer questions from our Telegraph Recommended Reader Panel.

Who inspired you to get into weightlifting?

Olamilekan, South East

Originally, it was lots of different people, particularly general gym goers who were doing weightlifting at my gym. As I’ve grown as an athlete and become more competitive, I’ve had other inspirations.

Most notably, coming into [the Commonwealth Games], it has to be Gareth [Evans], our coach. Looking back at his performance in 2018 when he won his gold medal is so inspiring. [English lifter] Emily Godley was another competitor in 2018. She won the gold medal in my category and I just remember thinking that she was on fire that day.

What are the best exercises for you to build muscle mass?

Norman, Wales

We spend a lot of time doing our main lifts, so snatches, clean and jerks, but we also do lots of pulls and squats. I spend a lot of time doing accessory work to make sure that my body stays healthy, especially being an older athlete. I’ve put on quite a lot of muscle in this last block just from going heavier and pushing my limits with my main lifts.

What advice would you give to people who want to improve their strength?

David, North West

The most important thing is consistency. As long as you’re doing something, do it regularly, even if it’s twice a week. Don’t be afraid of picking up some dumbbells. If you’ve got somebody that can teach you how to lift weights properly, that’s going to be the best option. Do it safely, do it consistently, and don’t be afraid to try new strength exercises.

News.title: Explosive mpox outbreak causes 3,000 cases in Madagascar
News.content:
More than 3,000 cases of mpox have been recorded in Madagascar after the virus spread from a single port city to some of the country’s busiest coastal hubs.

A total of 3,022 cases and 20 deaths have been recorded as of this week, with cases in Toamasina and Taolagnaro accounting for more than half of all diagnoses.

The outbreak has been linked to Clade 1b mpox, a strain that emerged in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2024, prompting the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare a global public health emergency at the time.

“The main factor driving the continued spread of the disease is human mobility, seeding new outbreaks in areas where the virus has not circulated before,” Professor Carlos Maluquer de Motes of the University of Surrey told The Telegraph.

“Under-reporting is likely, with the real number of cases exceeding what is being reported.”

News.title: Chelsea in 10-goal thriller as ‘Alonso ball’ brings risk and reward
News.content:
Chelsea’s first match under the management of Xabi Alonso was a 10-goal thriller in Australia, as the Premier League side eventually showed their class in a 6-4 win over Western Sydney Wanderers.

Star striker João Pedro, who was controversially left out of Brazil’s World Cup squad, scored a nine-minute hat-trick after coming off the bench with half an hour of the friendly remaining.

Alonso had selected a youthful team for the first hour before bringing nine senior players, including João Pedro, into the side in the second half. According to Transfermarkt, Chelsea’s squad is valued at over £1.3bn while their opponents a more modest £5.86m.

Teenage signing Dastan Satpayev, midfielder Dario Essugo and winger Jamie Gittens also found the net for Chelsea, who were defensively vulnerable for long spells for the game.

Here are five things Telegraph Sport learned from Alonso’s first match.

João Pedro picks up where he left off

João Pedro scored 13 goals in the second half of last season and his impressive performances resulted in the 24-year-old being named Chelsea’s player of the campaign. It was something of a surprise, then, when he was left out of Carlo Ancelotti’s Brazil squad this summer.

The good news for Chelsea is that João Pedro’s absence from the World Cup has given him plenty of time to recover ahead of the new campaign, and he looked thrillingly sharp in his second-half performance against Western Sydney Wanderers. The difference in class between João Pedro and Liam Delap, the man he replaced, was clear for all to see.

Two of the Brazilian’s three goals were classy, composed finishes — and he also created a goal for Gittens after surging past three defenders on the left wing. João Pedro looks like he means business.

Sports.title: World Cup winner Franco Baresi dies aged 66 as tributes flood in for Italy and AC Milan icon
Sports.content:
World Cup winner Franco Baresi dies aged 66 as tributes flood in for Italy and AC Milan icon

AC Milan legend and 1982 World Cup winner Franco Baresi has died at the age of 66, as tributes to the Italian legend land worldwide

View Image AC Milan and Italy legend Franco Baresi has died aged 66 (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

Franco Baresi has died at the age of 66, as the world of football mourns one of Italy's greatest-ever talents. The Travagilato-born talent will be remembered for a trophy-laden 20-year career with AC Milan, as well as a sensational international career culminating in winning the 1982 World Cup.

‌



A statement from I Rossoneri confirming the news of Baresi's passing read: "Announcing the loss of someone who embodied the heart and soul of AC Milan, is incredibly difficult. But everyone at the Club and all the Milanisti must live up to Franco Baresi's memory.

‌



"We must be strong and gather every bit of energy, even at this saddest of times. We lost Franco only a few months after his last public appearance in a packed San Siro, at the Milan Winter Olympics opening ceremony, an event on the world stage he helped make unforgettable.

‌



"In memory of Franco, we stand united, knowing he'll guide and push us throughout our Rossoneri journey. Forever. Because Baresi is forever."

A number of other Serie A clubs have also paid tribute to Baresi in a showing of solidarity with AC Milan, as well as the former centre-half's family and friends. Juventus wrote: "There are people who, with their talent, enter history. And others who, with their humanity, remain there forever.

"Franco Baresi was both. Class, style, leadership, and respect on and off the field. An example for generations of players and fans, loved and admired by all football enthusiasts.

‌



"His memory will live on forever. Juventus Football Club stands in solidarity with the Baresi family and @acmilan in this moment of profound sorrow."

Lazio added: "S.S. Lazio joins the family's mourning for the passing of Franco Baresi, the unforgettable defensive bastion of the Italian National Team and of Milan."

Napoli wrote: "President Aurelio De Laurentiis, Mr. Allegri, the executives, and all of SSC Napoli express their deepest condolences for the passing of Franco Baresi, a flag and legend of Milan and of the entire panorama of Italian football. To his family, the sincerest closeness from the entire Azzurri club."

‌



Roma said: "AS Roma joins in the mourning for the passing of Franco Baresi, who with his career left an indelible mark on the history of football. The Club stands in solidarity with the grief of his family and loved ones."

Sports.title: Eddie Howe gets England job verdict as Thomas Tuchel stance taken after Newcastle bombshell
Sports.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Eddie Howe gets England job verdict as Thomas Tuchel stance taken after Newcastle bombshell

Eddie Howe is out of work after deciding to leave Newcastle just weeks before the new season starts and the former Bournemouth boss has been linked with the England job

View 4 Images Eddie Howe is likely to have plenty of interest when he decides to return to management (Image: Kieran McManus/Shutterstock)

Former England striker Emile Heskey believes Eddie Howe would be perfect for the Three Lions job if Thomas Tuchel left his post at St George's Park. However, he backs Tuchel to take the national team forward and learn from any mistakes that cost them in the World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina.

‌



Englishman Howe has surprisingly ended his five-year spell at Newcastle United just under three weeks before the new Premier League season kicks off on August 21. The North East side have endured a torrid time recently with their best players poached amid the club's battle to meet their financial fair play requirements.

‌



Star striker Alexander Isak completed a British-record £125million switch to Liverpool last summer. That has been followed in recent months by the departures of winger Anthony Gordon to Barcelona and midfielder Sandro Tonali to Tottenham Hotspur.

‌



Alan Shearer shares honest take on Eddie Howe’s Newcastle exit and selling best players READ MORE :

Eddie Howe was FAILED by Newcastle United owners - he should have walked away earlier READ MORE :

Now, fan-favourite Bruno Guimaraes has been the latest player to be linked with a St James' Park departure. Arsenal are reportedly set to make a £70m offer for the Brazilian midfielder, in what would be another huge blow to Newcastle.

And Heskey, who starred for Liverpool, Aston Villa and several other clubs during his career, has now shared his view on the chaos at Newcastle as he speaks exclusively to Mirror Football on Howe's shock exit.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"It's obviously not great for the players, not great for the club," Heskey said. "I think he would have seen something and looked at how far he's brought them, and he's done a fantastic job to bring them to where he's brought them, but there is a ceiling, I think, within the club.

"And then missing out on transfers and not being able to get the players that he wants, and still having to try and push for Champions League, still trying to push for more and more.

"I think he's just probably looked at it and said he's taken them as far as you possibly can within the confines of financial fair play and what the club can actually do.

‌



"He's done a fantastic job, to be honest. He's won a trophy and that's one of the things that the club would have put on him and he's done that."

View 4 Images Eddie Howe has walked away from Newcastle United (Image: MI News/NurPhoto)

The 48-year-old has previously been linked with the England job after earning admirers for his work at Newcastle and Bournemouth. Howe has also worked with FA chief football officer Dan Ashworth at St James' Park.

‌



"The reality is that he's the best fit," Heskey admits. "When you're looking at an English manager with the best CV and the most experience. The only thing is, it's one thing being a club manager when you're so used to being with the players 24/7, moulding them into what you want.

"Then you're bringing them all from different places and trying to integrate them and get them to play the way that you want within 10 days. It's very tough. He will have some time off because I don't think Tuchel's going anywhere too soon.

"If you're looking at club management, I would have definitely said Chelsea would have been a decent fit before they got [Xabi] Alonso. I think he does really well with younger players.

‌



"He pushes them and drives them to do the best and not rest on their laurels. A lot of young lads, can at times rest on their laurels: 'We've done good, we've had one good game.' No, he will be pushing them. It's not one good game. It's a whole career. He's definitely one of those who will push them."

Newcastle are expected to appoint Al-Ahli boss Matthias Jaissle as Howe's successor. The German has a huge task to restore the Magpies' confidence before their season opener at home to Liverpool on August 23.

‌



"There was so much promise when the owners came in because they've got so much money to spend, but they can't spend the money," Heskey said. "You've got to balance the books and balancing the books means actually selling some of your best players.

"Aston Villa are in a similar boat. They're having to sell so many of the best young players; you don't really want to sell them, but it's just to balance the books. That's the tough side of it, where you're sitting there with an owner that wants to buy players, wants to invest money, but just can't do it.

"They've got a really huge fan base up there. They get their stadium rocking, but they just can't spend the money that they would want to do to challenge with the top four. Become the force that [Manchester] City are.

‌



"It's difficult to say where they will be this season. Mid-table will probably be good. When you're just losing all your best players, mid-table is probably going to be your best ask.

"It's gonna be tough and it's going to be a lot of pressure on some of these young lads, and it's sad that they're having to sell in the way that they're having to sell."

View 4 Images Bruno Guimaraes could be the next player to leave Newcastle (Image: Matt McNulty/Getty Images)

‌



While attention is returning to the club game, England fans and players will still feel some disappointment after their 2-1 defeat to Argentina in the World Cup semi-finals. Tuchel has been heavily criticised for his approach during the closing stages after the Three Lions went 1-0 up through Anthony Gordon, but Heskey believes the players must also take some responsibility.

"Look, everyone's disappointed," he says. "You've got to remember there's sometimes mentality and sometimes thought process, everything just goes out the window. This is where I say we need leaders as well, because you can tell me one thing and if it's difficult, if it's different on the pitch, I've got to be able to change that myself.

"I've played in teams where we change certain things because it's just not working and you could see it wasn't working. So why not change it? Why not, on the pitch, change it? I'm a centre forward. I hold the ball up, and I run the channels. I make and create fouls.

‌



"I give ourselves a little bit of breathing space. We didn't have any of that. Everything kept on coming back in.

"It's common sense sometimes and I'm not blaming the players as such, but they've got to take some blame as well. They've got to be held accountable as well because you're on the pitch. Sometimes I might see something from the side that is totally different to when you're actually in the heat of the battle, and you need those leaders to say, 'do this, step up there,' because you just hold the ball up, just do this or just do that.

"I played with lower teams, so we've had to do that. Playing against bigger teams and you're winning 1-0, and you're thinking how are we going to hold on to this? You do that up there; we'll do this here. Make sure you win this. Make sure you do that, and you're just constantly marshalling each other around."

‌



View 4 Images England's mentality against Argentina has been questioned (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

Heskey has called for perspective on Tuchel amid calls in some quarters for his sacking. He added: "I don't think he's done a bad job if I'm honest with you. I think he picked the right players.

"There might have been a case of having, maybe a Harry Maguire. If it's right at the death, there's someone who's going to put their head on the ball, I'm pretty sure he would have.

Article continues below

"But he chose who he chose. He stood by that and you've got to respect that. We got to the semifinals. Maybe a little bit of a change in mentality, and he understands the mentality of the players more and more now in those dark situations where your back's against the wall.

"I'm disappointed because you want to go to the final, but I'm not disappointed in the same way as everyone else is."

However, Michael Carrick's move into the dugout has led two club icons to believe there is an opportunity for Rashford to revive his United career next season.

‌



Man Utd open to offers for four more players as Michael Carrick wields transfer axe READ MORE :

Former midfielder Paul Ince believes Rashford would respond well to playing under Carrick, with the pair having previously been United teammates and also working together during the manager’s earlier coaching roles at Old Trafford. "I think Carrick can get the best out of him. I really, really do," Ince told Oddschecker.

"If Carrick just puts his arm around him and says, 'Yeah, listen, you know, I want you at the club, I need you at the club. This is where you’re going to play. This is what you’re going to do.' Then I believe you’re going to see a very, very good Rashford for Manchester United."

Ince’s thoughts are echoed by former United defender Wes Brown. The five-time Premier League winner is confident that Carrick would welcome Rashford back into his squad, given what the former Barcelona loanee can add to his attack.

‌



View 2 Images Michael Carrick and Rashford were previously teammates at United (Image: Matthew Peters/Manchester United via Getty Images)

“I’m sure Michael Carrick would love him back because it gives him another option,” Brown told The Sun on behalf of LiveFootballTickets. “If he could come into the scene this season, that helps out massively.

“I’m still not sure what’s going to happen, but I think if it was just up to Michael, he would definitely be back in. Obviously Marcus would have loved to have probably stayed at Barca.

‌



“They went another way, so I’m not sure what other options there is really. For me, it’s always time. People always fall out and you can always rekindle things in football. It’s just the way it is. I think it’ll be a boost for Michael for him to be here next season.”

Rashford has two years remaining on his United contract. The forward has made 426 appearances for his boyhood club, scoring 138 goals and registering 79 assists.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola's dream Joe Gomez replacement as Liverpool boss signs £40m former player
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola's dream Joe Gomez replacement as Liverpool boss signs £40m former player

Andoni Iraola is already feeling the pressure of dealing with another Liverpool injury crisis in defence

View 3 Images James Hill of Bournemouth would be a great signing for Liverpool (Image: Getty )

Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool tenure almost got off to a perfect start last week. The Reds emerged 4-2 victors against Sunderland in their pre-season friendly.

‌



Yet the win was overshadowed, and their summer preparations were hampered by an injury to Joe Gomez. The 29-year-old started the game as centre-back and captain but went off injured in just the eighth minute.

‌



Gomez travelled back to the club’s base in Chicago after the match and will undergo tests to determine the extent of the damage on what appeared to be another muscle injury.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Iraola was perfectly clear about how huge a blow it was, calling it “the worst news”. Ordinarily, an injury picked up in a friendly would have been enough cause for disappointment. But the Basque manager’s frustration was compounded by the fact he already finds his defence threadbare - despite the campaign not having got underway yet.

Skipper Virgil van Dijk missed the friendly after being given extra time off following the Netherlands’ World Cup campaign. New signing Jeremy Jacquet, who is expected to partner the Dutchman once the campaign begins, did not feature either as a precautionary measure.

‌



And £26m signing Giovanni Leoni is still rehabilitating for the foreseeable future as he works his way back from a serious ACL injury. Such a dearth of defenders meant Mor Talla Ndiaye, 18, and Ifeanyi Ndukwe, 18, made their debuts and both performed admirably given the situation.

But neither can be expected to feature regularly yet, and being forced to play them is hardly a good sign. As such, with Liverpool’s Premier League opener at Newcastle United less than a month away, Iraola will be desperate to add a central defender before the transfer window shuts on September 1.

View 3 Images Joe Gomez's injury has left Iraola light (Image: Getty )

‌



Given first-choice right-back Conor Bradley is set to miss a huge chunk of the season with his own knee injury, the Reds would be wise to look for a central defender who can also play right-back.

While there are many defenders on the market, signing one who can step into Iraola’s system seamlessly, requires no time to adapt to the pace of the Premier League, and still represents good value for money, is a difficult task.

Enter James Hill of Bournemouth. The 24-year-old is a player Iraola already knows well and trusts from his time with the Cherries.

‌



Hill was one of his most reliable defenders last season, having made 29 appearances in the league. The Englishman was a rock at the back, making 11.16 defensive contributions per 90 and winning 65.5% of his aerial duels as well as 63.8% of his duels overall.

No central defender managed to win more aerial duels per 90 in the league than Hill (4.88). He also showcased an ability to use the ball progressively in the manner Iraola demands from his centre-backs, creating an impressive 0.56 chances per 90.

View 3 Images Iraola and Hill enjoyed success together (Image: Getty )

‌



Centre-back is undoubtedly Hill's best position and he would slot in brilliantly alongside Van Dijk or Jacquet. Crucially, he also made three appearances at right-back last term, demonstrating his versatility. He is clearly a player that would bolster Iraola’s defence once more - this time in Liverpool's colours.

But despite a breakout season, there has been virtually zero transfer noise around Hill as of yet, meaning Liverpool have work to do if they want to land his signature. Bournemouth will want to hang onto their best players this summer, with new Cherries manager Marco Rose recently labelling him a "crucial player" for the club going forward.

As such, Liverpool would need to fork out a minimum fee of £40m - no small sum considering their other likely signings - to bring him to Anfield. But that is a fee worth paying, given the repercussions of another injury crisis at Liverpool this season would be calamitous.

‌



Another hurdle Liverpool’s negotiating team would have to navigate is convincing Hill to leave the Vitality Stadium. While that would ordinarily not have been too difficult, the defender recently heaped praise on his new manager Rose and is clearly relishing the chance to play European football next season.

He may also be tentative about coming in as a back-up, given Liverpool’s other defenders will eventually return to fitness. Hill may need assurances from Iraola about his game time, especially as he plays such a key role at Bournemouth and is tipped to be a future England international if he continues in this fashion.

Nevertheless, these are issues clubs face in most transfer dealings. Liverpool's ideal defensive signing is clear to see - all that remains now is for the club to move swiftly in order to give Iraola the best chance of success this season.

Sports.title: FIFA issues new defiant statement after UEFA threatens to boycott World Cup
Sports.content:
FIFA issues new defiant statement after UEFA threatens to boycott World Cup

FIFA have insisted that “nobody is selling football” after UEFA threatens to boycott the World Cup due to Infantino's sale plans

View 2 Images FIFA issues new statement after UEFA threatens to boycott World Cup (Image: BSR Agency, Getty Images)

FIFA have issued a new defiant statement insisting “nobody is selling football” after UEFA threatened to boycott the World Cup.

‌



Despite the criticism of its decision to launch a consultation on selling stakes in a World Cup commercial entity to private investors, FIFA is not withdrawing the plan.

‌



Although the association have asserted they are not "selling football" in their latest statement, the consultation period will go ahead.

‌



When plans to created FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) first emerged in media reports in The Times and the Financial Times on Tuesday UEFA reacted furiously.

UEFA's 55 member associations said they would boycott the World Cup and not participate in any FIFA tournament until the plan was withdrawn.

Gianni Infantino MUST GO - FIFA chief has no way back after brutal response to World Cup plot READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino's plan for World Cup explained as FIFA put on notice over boycott READ MORE :

In a statement released on Friday morning, FIFA said: “We have heard the feedback provided by the respective confederations in relation to the proposed establishment of FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) and would like to address the issues that have surfaced since the initial media reporting on Tuesday.

‌



“We respect the feedback and concern aired in public and reaffirm our commitment to an open and democratic consultation.

⁠”Our planned consultation process was disrupted by incorrect media reports. We will proceed with this consultation process to ensure that each MA has the ability to express its vote based on facts.”

The statement continued: “FFE has been proposed solely to ensure that all FIFA Member Associations (MAs) have the opportunity to take meaningful ownership of the commercial opportunity of football in their respective countries, and that this does not come at the cost of either the spirit or the governance of FIFA or football itself. Nobody is selling football. This is not something FIFA would ever entertain.”

‌



View 2 Images As well as England, World Cup winners Spain are also included in the boycott (Image: David Ramos/Getty Images)

CONCACAF, the confederation representing 41 nations from North and Central America, along with the Caribbean, also made clear its opposition to FIFA’s plan, saying it “rejected the proposal”.

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has publicly backed the plan, with an investor group led by Thrive Eternal, founded by Joshua Kushner – the brother of United States President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner – waiting in the wings to secure a minority stake in the new venture.

‌



However, as European teams threaten to withdraw their involvement in tournaments the promises of huge returns to national associations if FFE goes ahead are unlikely to be honoured.

European and world leagues are also opposed to the plans – fearing that commercial imperatives will drive FIFA to hold bigger and more frequent tournaments in the future, eating even further into domestic schedules.

UEFA’s opposition to the plan, in its words, is “unanimous and unequivocal”.

‌



The European football’s governing body stated: “No UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership."

FIFA’s statement added that “each MA should be allowed to review the proposal and have a say in shaping their own future”.

The Andoni Iraola era at Liverpool has begun and the new manager brings with him a wave of changes. But so far, only two new recruits have arrived at Anfield in Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz.

‌



After leaving Bournemouth for the Reds, Iraola's pre-season is in full swing and Liverpool followed up a win against Sunderland with a 1-0 victory over Wrexham in New York. Rio Ngumoha's strike was the difference and he notably played out on the right wing, where the iconic Mohamed Salah would usually prowl. The Egyptian King has still not been replaced.

‌



However, Liverpool's transfer window could soon enter overdrive as they pick up their pursuit of PSG's Bradley Barcola, and they've been given a huge boost. Mirror Football takes a look at the latest transfer updates surrounding Anfield.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Bradley Barcola boost

It is understood that Liverpool have begun negotiations with PSG over Barcola, who is valued at an eye-watering £140m. Preliminary talks with the player's representatives have already been held and the signs are encouraging.

Jamie Carragher highlights major Bradley Barcola concern as Liverpool make move for star READ MORE :

Liverpool takeover plan clear as billionaires approached over buying stake from FSG READ MORE :

However, it is likely the French side will want a replacement before they let a player like Barcola walk. Sky Sports Germany reports that a decisive development has taken place in talks regarding Maghnes Akliouche.

Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Lewis Hall transfer update emerges as defender completes move

Manchester United have been linked with a move for Newcastle's Lewis Hall as the club's busy summer transfer window continues

View 2 Images Manchester United have been linked with Newcastle United's Lewis Hall (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Manchester United are seeking new signings to strengthen their squad. Michael Carrick’s side are preparing for a pivotal campaign that will see the club return to the Champions League and look to be part of the Premier League title race.

‌



Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans are the club’s most notable new additions so far as United seek to reshape their midfield. The Red Devils spent a combined £85million on the duo but have been linked with signing a third midfielder this summer.

‌



Despite the focus on midfield, Carrick will be aware of the need to strengthen other areas of his team. The club are interested in Newcastle left-back Lewis Hall, who is reportedly open to a move to Old Trafford.

‌



Meanwhile, United have confirmed that an academy graduate has left the club and have been linked with further outgoings. Here, Mirror Football looks at some of the biggest stories surrounding the club.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Lewis Hall transfer update

United are interested in Newcastle defender Hall and are reportedly considering a move for the full-back. The update follows news on Thursday morning that that Eddie Howe had left Newcastle, ending the manager’s almost five-year reign at St James’ Park.

‌



Man Utd ready to offload quartet including player they refused to swap for Carlos Baleba READ MORE :

Man United slammed by Gary Neville over failure to land no-brainer Chelsea signing READ MORE :

The Sun reports that United are “weighing up” a move for Hall, given the uncertainty around the Magpies. However, it is claimed that the England international may yet be persuaded to stay, depending on Howe’s successor.

From United’s standpoint, the former Chelsea academy graduate is viewed as a long-term successor to Luke Shaw at left-back. However, Newcastle may be reluctant to sell another key player after losing Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali this summer, while Bruno Guimaraes has also attracted interest.

United have confirmed that young defender Tyler Fredricson has completed a permanent move to Swiss side Lausanne-Sport. The 21-year-old centre-back made four senior appearances for United after rising through the club’s academy ranks. The statement added: “Joining the club at Under-9 level, Tyler has been a model professional throughout his time with the club and a popular member of our Academy squads. His place in United’s history books is also secured as a recipient of the prestigious Denzil Haroun Reserve-Team Player of the Year award in 2025.

“Lausanne finished ninth in the Swiss Super League last season, and they hope to progress this term following July’s appointment of new head coach Luka Elsner. Everybody at United thanks Tyler for all his efforts during his time with the club and we wish him all the best for the next chapter of his career.”

Sports.title: FIFA: Nobody is selling football
Sports.content:
FIFA insists "nobody is selling football" amid criticism of its decision to launch a consultation on selling stakes in a World Cup commercial entity to private investors.

However, football's global governing body stopped short of withdrawing the controversial plan and insisted it would press ahead with the consultation period.

UEFA reacted furiously when the plans to create FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) first emerged in media reports in The Times and the Financial Times on Tuesday.

Less than 48 hours later, UEFA's 55 member associations insisted they would not participate in any FIFA tournament until the plan was withdrawn. CONCACAF, the confederation representing 41 nations from North and Central America, along with the Caribbean, also made clear its opposition to FIFA's plan, saying it "rejected the proposal".

In a statement released on Friday morning, FIFA said: "We have heard the feedback provided by the respective confederations in relation to the proposed establishment of FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) and would like to address the issues that have surfaced since the initial media reporting on Tuesday.

"We respect the feedback and concern aired in public and reaffirm our commitment to an open and democratic consultation.

⁠"Our planned consultation process was disrupted by incorrect media reports. We will proceed with this consultation process to ensure that each MA has the ability to express its vote based on facts."

The statement continued: "FFE has been proposed solely to ensure that all FIFA Member Associations (MAs) have the opportunity to take meaningful ownership of the commercial opportunity of football in their respective countries, and that this does not come at the cost of either the spirit or the governance of FIFA or football itself.

"Nobody is selling football. This is not something FIFA would ever entertain."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kaveh explains why FIFA president Infantino is under serious pressure after UEFA said it will boycott FIFA tournaments if the proposal to sell off a stake in the World Cup goes ahead and CONCACAF also rejected the idea of the proposals

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has publicly backed the plan, with an investor group led by Thrive Eternal, founded by Joshua Kushner - the brother of United States President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner - waiting in the wings to secure a minority stake in the new venture.

However, promises of huge returns to national associations if FFE goes ahead could surely not be honoured if the men's and women's World Cups took place without European involvement, even if Infantino could still muster majority support for FFE.

European and world leagues are also opposed to the plans - fearing that commercial imperatives will drive FIFA to hold bigger and more frequent tournaments in the future, eating even further into domestic schedules.

UEFA's opposition to the plan, in its words, is "unanimous and unequivocal".

"No UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership," European football's governing body stated.

FIFA's statement added that "each MA should be allowed to review the proposal and have a say in shaping their own future".

'Infantino is in a hole and he needs to stop digging'

Analysis from Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol:

"It is a desperate, tone-deaf statement that was issued in the middle of the night from FIFA's Zurich bunker. It's very interesting that it doesn't mention their president by name.

"The way I read this is that this is a statement from Gianni Infantino; it's not necessarily a FIFA statement. How many people inside FIFA actually agree with what he is doing?

"He's in a hole and he needs to stop digging. He needs to start reading the room. He needs to start accepting the fact his power is starting to ebb away and he needs to start by apologising to football, to football fans all around the world - and he also needs to start apologising and explain himself to the confederations and the presidents of the 211 member associations.

"And he needs to stop blaming the media. What is this crazy obsession he's got? He seems to have picked it up from President Donald Trump, where he thinks it's a good idea to keep lashing out at the media. He seems to somehow think that is going to help him.

"The reporting that has been done this week, which was led by The Times and the Financial Times has been completely and utterly accurate. And if it wasn't for this reporting, there wouldn't be this furore that we have now and we wouldn't know the facts we know now.

"I suggest Infantino needs to change course. He needs to wake up and fully understand the mess he has created for himself and he needs to start saying sorry because I think that's the only way he's going to be able to save himself."

Sports.title: Fowler, Cantlay impress as Malnati leads after threatening 59 round
Sports.content:
Rickie Fowler and Patrick Cantlay are in contention after the first round of the Rocket Classic in Detroit as leader Peter Malnati threatened a sensational sub-60 score.

Malnati shot a career-best nine-under 61 to tie the tournament's record for the first round to take a two-shot lead over Fowler and Ryan Gerard, with Cantlay and Patrick Fishburn another shot back.

When Malnati stood on the first tee, his caddie suggested leaving the driver in his bag to play it safe and set up a solid start.

Malnati, though, went against the advice and used his driver to put a tee shot in the middle of the fairway that set up his first of seven birdies on the front nine.

"Even in the beginning before I knew it was going to be a special day, I didn't feel the same level of like anxiety," he said.

"I don't think I took advantage of a super easy course. I played great."

Image: Peter Malnati hits from the 18th tee during the first round of the Rocket Classic (AP Photo/Jose Juarez)

With thoughts of a sub-60 round crossing his mind, he made a 55-foot putt for birdie at the 11th and was nine under through 13 holes before missing some putts down the stretch in a bogey-free round.

Detroit Golf Club underwent a $16 million renovation, including converting a couple of par-5 holes into par-4s and adding a lot of bunkers, in an attempt to restore Donald Ross' vision for it more than a century ago, while making it more challenging.

Fowler and Ryan Gerard shot 63s, putting them two shots back and one stroke ahead of Cantlay and Fishburn.

Michael Brennan surged up the leaderboard after starting two over through four holes with eight straight birdies - one shy of the PGA Tour record.

He finished with a 65, putting him four strokes back with a pack of players that includes Keegan Bradley, who appeared to be mocked by some spectators who pretended he hit a hole in one on the par-three fifth.

Open runner-up Cameron Young has work to do on one under while US Open champion Wyndham Clark is on one over.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fans erupted as Keegan Bradley hit this tee shot on the fifth hole of the Rocket Classic despite the ball not going in!

Despite significant changes at the course, Malnati and many other players still went low at a tournament that has been a birdie fest since 2019, when a Detroit-based mortgage company ended a decade-long drought in Michigan without a PGA Tour stop that dated to Tiger Woods winning the last Buick Open.

The PGA Tour is moving to a new model for 2028, effectively creating two tours, and Detroit organizers are taking an exit. The Rocket Classic wasn't interested in continuing to spend $15 million a year to be part of the second tier and didn't want to double the costs to be part of the elite tier.

"It's definitely been a bummer to kind of come into this knowing it was the last one," said Fowler, a Rocket Mortgage spokesman and the tournament's 2023 champion.

Sports.title: Huddersfield beat Hull FC in bottom-of-the-table clash
Sports.content:
Super League: Huddersfield Giants beat Hull FC 22-16 in bottom of the table clash for second straight win

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Huddersfield Giants against Hull FC from the Super League Highlights of Huddersfield Giants against Hull FC from the Super League

Huddersfield twice came from behind and produced a second-half fightback as they picked up a second straight Betfred Super League victory with a 22-16 win over Hull FC at the Accu Stadium.

Following their win over York last week, Huddersfield registered back-to-back victories for the first time since April. They remain rock-bottom of the table but are now just two points behind losers Hull.

Huddersfield were on the front foot after being given a fresh set of six around 40 metres out and they made Hull pay after an inside ball from Harry Rushton was given to Chris Patolo who reached out across the whitewash. George Flanagan converted.

Hull managed to get themselves on level terms midway through the first half, Jake Arthur delivered a short ball to Joe Batchelor who was able to race clear and slide over.

The visitors took the lead just six minutes later following an excellent break by Cade Cust who had Ethan O'Neill and Davy Litten for support, and he was able to finish off in the corner but Zak Hardaker was unable to add the extras.

Huddersfield almost had their second try before the break but Jacob Gagai was unable to dot down in the corner and was denied a try following a video review.

Much like the first half, the hosts made a strong start to the second and had the opening try of the period, Tui Lolohea's kick forced a Hull knock-on and Connor Wrench was able to kick through before grounding behind the sticks.

Huddersfield's George Flanagan played a key role to help his side to victory (Picture by Allan McKenzie/SWpix.com)

Their lead was short-lived though, as Hull turned defence into attack with a break down the field courtesy of O'Neill and he offloaded to Litten who finished off the move to make it 16-12.

Huddersfield bit back once again when Lewis Jagger dived over to make it a level game and after Hull were pulled for a high tackle, the home side went down the other end and got the winning try when Flanagan dived behind the posts to pick up another vital win.

"It was nice to have a bit of belief at the back end of the game and find a way to win instead of lose," Huddersfield head coach Jim Lenihan told Sky Sports.

"It's the reward of a lot of hard work in training. The biggest part is we are looking forward to playing football. This is a very proud club that works hard behind the scenes, we want to walk round with some pride about ourselves."

Sports.title: England fight back to reach netball semi-finals at Commonwealth Games
Sports.content:
England fought back to beat South Africa 58-54 to reach the netball semi-finals at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

Both sides needed to win to book a spot in the last four and England roared back from an early 17-11 deficit after the first quarter to keep their hopes of a second Commonwealth gold alive.

The Vitality Roses will face New Zealand in the second of Saturday's semi-finals after Australia play Jamaica, then the gold and bronze-medal matches take place on Sunday.

"Shout out to Halimat Adio. She was unreal in that second quarter. So proud of her to bring us that energy and get us back in the game when we needed it," captain Francesca Williams told TNT Sports.

"We have been under pressure all week to perform so for us to finish out a game like that and ride the wave of goal for goal in the last quarter and come out on top, I'm so proud."

Image: Halimat Adio player a pivotal role for England to slow down South Africa's Elmere van der Berg (PA)

England got off to a nervy start as South Africa goal shooter Elmere van der Berg came flying out of the blocks with 16 goals from 19 attempts which silenced the crowd at the OVO Hydro.

Halimat Adio and Funmi Fadoju came on, which tightened up England's defence, and it changed the momentum of the match as they slowly got themselves back into the contest to trail just 29-28 at half-time.

England went on a charge early in the third quarter with five consecutive goals to move 35-30 ahead and took a 45-41 lead into the last quarter.

Image: The Duke and Duchess of Edinburgh attended the match (PA)

As the clock ran down, England calmly maintained their slender four-goal advantage as Olivia Tchine and Lois Pearson kept their composure up front to get Anna Stembridge's side over the line.

Stembridge stepped up to become head coach just four months before the Commonwealth Games after Jess Thirlby resigned.

Netball has been in the Commonwealth Games since 1998 but England have never won a medal when it has been held in the United Kingdom.
