Sports.title: Marcus Rashford sends emotional message to Barcelona fans ahead of expected return to Manchester United - after Spanish giants rejected chance to sign him for £26m
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford has sent a farewell message to Barcelona as the countdown continues towards his return to Manchester United.

Rashford spent last season on loan at the Nou Camp, contributing 14 goals and 14 assists as the Catalans won La Liga and reached the quarter-finals of the Champions League.

However, Barca decided not to trigger an option to buy him from United for £26million before a deadline in mid-June, and signed Newcastle’s Anthony Gordon for £70m.

On Thursday, Rashford posted a picture on social media of his No.14 shirt and another of him in action for the club with the message: ‘I am extremely grateful to everyone at the club for making my time here a positive and unforgettable experience. I enjoyed every moment, and I will keep many special memories. I wish the club and all its fans every success in the coming season. Visca Barca!’

Rashford is now set to rejoin United where he has a contract until June 2028 worth around £315,000-a-week. The England international is having some time off after helping England reach the World Cup semi-finals, and it remains to be seen if he will be involved in United’s training camp in Ireland next month which includes a friendly against Leeds at Croke Park on August 12.

With United in need of a left-sided attacker, and Rashford contracted to his boyhood club for another two seasons, it makes sense for the 28-year-old to come back and play under head coach Michael Carrick.

Marcus Rashford has sent a farewell message following his season long loan at Barcelona

It is looking increasingly like Rashford will be at Man United when the transfer window closes

There is no chance of a repeat of last summer when the more confrontational Ruben Amorim placed him in a ‘bomb squad’ of five players who trained separately from the main group at Carrington before Rashford left for Barcelona.

After initially putting a price of £40m on their top-earner this summer in the hope of moving him off the wage bill, it has been difficult for United to find a club willing to pay more than the £26m stipulated in the Barca loan as well as Rashford’s salary.

The club also discovered the high cost of replacing him when one option, West Ham’s Crysencio Summerville, joined Al-Hilal for £60m.

There is still time for some twists and turns before the window closes on September 1, but it’s looking increasingly likely that Rashford will be at United when it does.

Sports.title: Chaos at the Commonwealth Games as HUGE crash in wheelchair race forces organisers to order a re-run as England star is left 'traumatised' at thought of losing medal
Sports.content:
Chaos at the Commonwealth Games as HUGE crash in wheelchair race forces organisers to order a re-run as England star is left 'traumatised' at thought of losing medal

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

England’s Ellis Kottas was left ‘lowkey traumatised’ at the prospect of losing her silver medal after Commonwealth chiefs ordered a re-race following a mass wheelchair crash.

Four out of seven athletes finished women’s T54 1500m final on Wednesday night after four crashes, three overturned wheelchairs and a disqualification.

Scotland’s Melanie Woods finished first with Commonwealth record of 3min 33.39sec but the athletes were told the following morning that they must race again.

Kottas said: ‘While I’m lowkey traumatised if I’m going to medal I want to do so on my own merit, so I will go out and give it all I’ve got. If I don’t medal so be it, I’ll still have the incredible memories of lifting that England flag.'

The decision was criticised by Team England’s chef de mission, Jonny Riall, who said: ‘We are incredibly disappointed by the late decision. While there is no formal protest process available to us, we have strongly challenged the decision.

A huge crash out on the first bend of the women's 1500m T54 final 😬 pic.twitter.com/wWNxhKIGqb — TNT Sports (@tntsports) July 29, 2026

Four out of seven athletes finished women’s T54 1500m final on Wednesday night after four crashes, three overturned wheelchairs and a disqualification

'While I really don’t want to rerun the race (lowkey traumatised) if I’m going to medal I want to do so on my own merit,' silver medallist Ellis Kottas said

'The race officials did not halt the race at the time of the incident, nor was any immediate decision made to declare the race void or order a rerun.

'Our priority is the welfare of our athletes. We will now do everything we can do support Ellis during the extremely short turnaround.'

Compliments to the chef as Emily reigns supreme

Not since the Finnieston Crane was in action have Glasgow’s docklands witnessed such large masses of metal being thrown around.

Emily Campbell, with lions weaved into her red and white hair, shifted 278kg – 115 in the Snatch and 163 in the Clean and Jerk – to win gold with a record Commonwealth lift.

On the banks of the River Clyde, England’s Olympian showed her adoring fans why she is regarded as the sport’s great entertainer.

She blew kisses to the crowd and told her rivals that there is ‘life in this old bird yet’ before collecting her medal from the Duchess of Edinburgh.

It takes thousands of calories to fuel a weightlifter and next month Campbell will continue to fly the flag for her sport when the takes part in Celebrity MasterChef.

‘MasterChef is definitely more nerve-racking!’ she laughed.

Emily Campbell, with lions weaved into her red and white hair, shifted 278kg – 115 in the Snatch and 163 in the Clean and Jerk – to win gold with a record Commonwealth lift

‘It’s really nice for me to do something without being Emily the weightlifter, to just do something as Emily. My signature dish is Caribbean and that’s all I’m going to give you because I want you to watch it! It’s another platform to put weightlifting in, another time for us to have that spotlight on us.

At 32, the weightlifting game is beginning taking its toll on her joints. Olympic gold still eludes her but she is yet to commit to competing at LA 2028.

‘We’ve got to look at the practicalities of LA,’ she said. ‘We have to do a slightly different qualification process to other sports. We’ve got to look at that and we can get our body through.

'If I go to LA, I would want to be in contention for a medal, so we want to make sure that that’s feasible. We just have to be very sensible about decisions and hopefully you’ll see me there.

'But for now, we enjoy what happened. We have some good food, maybe a few drinks. We're out in Glasgow!'

Sports.title: Donald Trump on collision course as FIFA's worst-case scenario over World Cup plans unfolds
Sports.content:
Donald Trump on collision course as FIFA's worst-case scenario over World Cup plans unfolds

Gianni Infantino's FIFA World Cup plans have been rejected by CONCACAF, which includes the United States, and could see the FIFA president forced into an awkward conversation with Donald Trump

View 2 Images Donald Trump has reportedly been briefed on FIFA's plans (Image: AP Photo/Alex Brandon)

U.S. Soccer, as part of CONCACAF, has publicly opposed Gianni Infantino's World Cup proposals, despite reports that President Donald Trump's administration had been briefed on the plans.

‌



The football federation for North and Central America, alongside the Caribbean, openly voiced its opposition to Infantino's vision, which sought to establish FIFA Forward Enterprise to consolidate FIFA's commercial operations, spanning sponsorship, ticketing, licensing and broadcasting - alongside tournament delivery.

‌



The scheme then involved offloading a minority stake, believed to be somewhere between 20 and 30 per cent, to private investors, including figures with connections to Trump. Joshua Kushner, brother of the US president's son-in-law Jared, was amongst the backers behind the proposal.

‌



The Trump administration was also thought to have been consulted regarding the scheme, which has been publicly rebuffed by UEFA, who declared it will boycott all FIFA competitions until the proposal is abandoned. While CONCACAF held back from threatening competition withdrawals, it has made its lack of support for the plan abundantly clear.

FIFA issues new defiant statement after UEFA threatens to boycott World Cup READ MORE :

Man Utd transfer talks confirmed as agent says deal is close READ MORE :

Following their own statement's release, US Soccer's X account emphasised their public resistance to Infantino.

It stated: "U.S. Soccer stands with Concacaf and its members," shortly after CONCACAF publicly declared they will not back Infantino's proposal.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Given that Trump's administration was consulted about the concept, the fact the US' equivalent to the Football Association has so openly rejected the scheme represents a setback to both Infantino and Trump and could force the pair into an uncomfortable discussion in the very near future.

Furthermore, the embattled FIFA president also indicated his proposal required backing from just over 50 per cent of FIFA's 211 member nations to proceed. With UEFA and CONCACAF already opposing it, he has already lost 96 nations (55 in UEFA and 41 in CONCACAF).

‌



View 2 Images Donald Trump spent plenty of time with Gianni Infantino (Image: Getty)

In their statement, the federation representing North and South America wrote: "Concacaf is a confederation united by the love of our game, where football comes first. Guided by this philosophy over the past ten years we have built, from the ground up, an organisation founded on service, transparent governance, and the long-term stewardship of football.

"History has shown FIFA and the football family what happens when the custodians of the game lose sight of these values. With this in mind, Concacaf today convened a meeting of the presidents of its 41 Member Associations, together with its President, Council members, and its FIFA Council members, to discuss a proposal developed and presented by the FIFA President to establish 'FIFA Forward Enterprise' and sell interests in the FIFA World Cup to private investors.

‌



"During the meeting, the membership expressed deep concerns about the lack of due process surrounding the proposal, the artificially short deadline imposed, and the absence of any review or approval by the relevant FIFA governance bodies. In addition, the need for private equity investment to fund new and existing FIFA Forward programs following the most profitable FIFA World Cup in history was questioned.

"The discussion reinforced the need for greater transparency and proper governance. For these reasons, Concacaf and its 41 Member Associations have: Rejected the proposal.

"Tasked their FIFA Council Members with engaging FIFA to determine how existing vast FIFA reserves could be used to increase FIFA Forward funding for football development across our region; and tasked their FIFA Council Members with instructing the FIFA President to ensure that any matter follows the proper governance processes via staff and FIFA Council, in accordance with the FIFA Statutes.

Article continues below

"Through these actions, Concacaf reaffirms that football's future-and its greatest asset-must remain in the hands of our football family."

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Bruno Guimaraes twist as Gunners issue major transfer hint
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Bruno Guimaraes twist as Gunners issue major transfer hint

Arsenal look set to be active in the transfer window before it slams shut

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta is not done adding to his Arsenal squad (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Arsenal may have moved a step closer in their chase of Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes. It's been a miserable summer for Magpies fans, who've witnessed the departures of Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali.

‌



A different kind of exit was confirmed on Thursday after news broke that Eddie Howe will leave the club after five years in charge. While devastating for those on the north east, it could spell good news for Gunners fans.

‌



Howe was desperate to keep Guimaraes at St James' Park this summer and his departure could cause a breakthrough in negotiations in regards to the Brazilian's future. Elsewhere, the Premier League champions themselves made an announcement which could bode well for the future.

‌



Mirror Football takes a look at the latest stories coming out of the Emirates Stadium...

Bruno Guimaraes transfer twist

View 3 Images Bruno Guimaraes is a top target for the Gunners (Image: Richard Pelham/Getty Images)

Arsenal's pursuit of Bruno Guimaraes has dominated the summer period, with the Gunners eager to add the Newcastle captain to their squad. A £70million deal for the Brazil international has yet to be agreed between the two clubs, who've yet to open direct negotiations with one another.

‌



The saga took another twist on Thursday after Eddie Howe's departure from St James' Park. According to The Telegraph, Howe had become extremely frustrated by the sales of Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali, as well as the continuing uncertainty over his captain's future.

While Guimaraes, 28, is set to return to Newcastle for pre-season training on Friday, conversations surrounding his exit or stay will only heat up following Howe's exit. The Brazilian has built up a close relationship with the Newcastle faithful, but is receptive to a move to London that would see him return to the Champions League.

Arsenal confirmation

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta could be set to welcome new signings at Arsenal (Image: Gareth Fuller/PA Wire)

‌



Unlike many clubs who usually keep their cards close to their chest when it comes to potential new signings, Arsenal have gone in the opposite direction. The Gunners took to their official club website to inform their fans that they will likely be making more summer acquisitions before the window slams shut.

In an article previewing their pre-season friendly against Girona on Saturday, a portion read: "Two new signings have also joined the group this pre-season – goalkeeper Illan Meslier and forward Christos Tzolis – with more expected to sign before the end of the transfer window."

Arteta himself teased the possibility about new incomings in an interview with Arsenal.com. The Spaniard said: "We all know about the context of this transfer window. From ownership to the board, the sporting director and myself, we know that we want to take this club to a different level.

"That is going to require a better squad, better individuals. We have identified where we have opportunities to grow and to improve and to evolve our game and what is going to be needed to achieve that. Hopefully very soon we can start to put things in a very concrete way."

Sports.title: Ex-Newcastle owner Amanda Staveley in talks to buy West Ham stake
Sports.content:
Ex-Newcastle owner Amanda Staveley in talks to buy West Ham stake

Amanda Staveley and her husband, Mehrdad Ghodoussi, sold their stake in Newcastle United two years ago but have set their sights on a return to football with West Ham

View 2 Images A consortium led by Amanda Staveley has held talks over buying a stake in West Ham (Image: Nigel French/PA Wire)

A consortium led by Amanda Staveley, the former co-owner of Newcastle United, is said to be 'close' to acquiring a 25 per cent stake in West Ham.

The Hammers were relegated from the Premier League last season and will now ply their trade in the Championship but that has not deterred interest from Staveley and her husband, Mehrdad Ghodoussi, in buying into the east London club following their departure from Newcastle two years ago.

PCP Capital Partners, Staveley and Ghodoussi's firm, have held talks over purchasing the shares previously held by the late David Gold.

The Times claim that a deal for Staveley's consortium to acquire the 25 per cent stake from Gold's daughter, Vanessa, is close following talks.

Chelsea, Sunderland and Nottingham Forest caught out as Premier League gambling ban bites READ MORE :

Arsenal close in on £80m Bruno Guimaraes transfer in major breakthrough for Mikel Arteta READ MORE :

Not only that, the report notes that if Staveley and Co are successful in their attempt to purchase a minority stake in the club then it could be followed by them presenting an offer for the shares owned by David Sullivan, which would give them majority control of the club.

Sullivan resigned as West Ham chairman last month in the wake of historic sexual allegations. A BBC Panorama investigation alleged that Mr Sullivan had preyed on women for sex. He has strenuously denied the allegations and said he will be launching legal action against the BBC.

Article continues below

Staveley's consortium is said to be backed by investors from the United States and the Far East who had initially considered bidding for one of West Ham's bitter rivals, Tottenham.

However, the consortium has designs on transforming West Ham's fortunes following relegation and there are plans to invest heavily in the playing squad.

View 2 Images Staveley was a pivotal figure behind Newcastle's Saudi-backed takeover (Image: Getty Images)

There are also ambitions to purchase the club's much maligned home ground, the London Stadium; talks have even already been held with officials connected to the London mayor’s office.

Thought Staveley's consortium hope to buy into the club, pre-emption rights means that West Ham's other major shareholder, Daniel Kretinsky, has first option to purchase the shares ahead of external parties.

He and Vanessa Gold had previously released a joint statement in June saying the Czech billionaire, who owns a 27 per cent stake in the club, had agreed a deal to purchase some of Gold's shares to increase his standing to "approximately 43 per cent".

Sports.title: UEFA have one problem in toppling Gianni Infantino from power at FIFA over World Cup plan
Sports.content:
UEFA have one problem in toppling Gianni Infantino from power at FIFA over World Cup plan

Gianni Infantino has seen his controversial plans backfire, with UEFA and CONCACAF rejecting the proposal, and now his future as FIFA president hangs in the balance

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino faces an uncertain future at FIFA after Aleksander Ceferin's UEFA challenged him (Image: Harry Murphy/UEFA via Getty Images)

Gianni Infantino's position as FIFA president is under threat after his plan to sell off the World Cup triggered a tremendous backlash - but a viable challenger to his throne is yet to emerge.

‌



European football's governing body UEFA met virtually on Thursday and, after a fiery meeting, fired out a powerful and damning statement which stated their willingness to boycott future FIFA tournaments.

‌



UEFA called Infantino's secretive behaviour around the proposal to invite third-party investment in tournaments "irresponsible and indefensible". And although it didn't name him, it accused Infantino of "a profound failure of leadership" and of seeing his first duty as "to maximise financial return".

‌



Infantino's attempts to effectively buy off FIFA members by offering $40m (£30m) if they back his plan have backfired spectacularly, with CONCACAF - North and Central America's governing body - following UEFA's lead later on Thursday. CONCACAF said it rejected the proposal, criticising the "lack of due process" at FIFA around the plans.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Gianni Infantino in trouble as new statement released after UEFA fury over World Cup plans READ MORE :

England and UEFA nations WILL BOYCOTT World Cup in protest over Gianni Infantino sale plan READ MORE :

UEFA and CONCACAF uniting in defiance of Infantino would appear to stop the plans dead in their tracks, while also throwing the Swiss bureaucrat's future as FIFA president into doubt.

‌



Just 13 days ago the Guardian reported that more than 200 of FIFA's 211 members had formally endorsed Infantino for re-election for a fourth term, having first taken control in 2016. He was set to run unchallenged and extend his reign at FIFA congress in March.

However, his barefaced attempts to sell off football in pursuit of enrichment, which appeared designed to buy support, may have torpedoed his efforts.

The only thing currently missing is a credible challenger. Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al-Khelaifi had garnered some support, but a source has said he has "absolutely no ambition, no intention, nor any interest in this role at FIFA".

‌



View 3 Images Nasser al-Khelaifi reportedly doesn't want to challenge Gianni Infantino (Image: LOU BENOIST/AFP via Getty Images)

He leads the European Football Clubs umbrella group, so already holds plenty of power of his own, having helped steady the ship after the failed European Super League coup in 2021.

UEFA chief Aleksander Ceferin has emerged as the biggest thorn in Infantino's side, having previously led the fightback against his proposal to stage the World Cup every two years. But the Slovenian reportedly also lacks the desire to mount a leadership challenge, unlike Infantino doesn't crave the limelight, and is happy at UEFA.

‌



Legia Warsaw president Dariusz Mioduski has been backed by the Belgian, Spanish, Norwegian, German and Swedish associations, according to a report from talkSPORT earlier this month. Meanwhile, CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani and Confederation of African Football (CAF) Patrice Motsepe may lack the desire to run against Infantino.

There is time for things to change, however with contenders given until November 18 to attract supporters and put forward their names.

View 3 Images Aleksander Ceferin is leading the backlash against Gianni Infantino (Image: Alexander Hassenstein, Getty Images)

‌



The fiery nature of UEFA's statement suggests they could be seeking regime change at FIFA. "We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA’s proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors," it reads.

"The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football’s greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale.

"It is both irresponsible and indefensible that a proposal of such significance for football was conceived in secret and brought to the brink of approval without any meaningful consultation with those entrusted with stewarding the game. This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of FIFA’s duty as the custodian of world football."

Article continues below

Time will tell if that "failure of leadership" leads to Infantino's downfall.

Sports.title: Man Utd transfer talks confirmed as agent says deal is close
Sports.content:
Man Utd transfer talks confirmed as agent says deal is close

Manchester United made an enquiry for Paraguay goalkeeper Orlando Gill, who starred at the World Cup, according to the player's agent - though a move to San Lorenzo now appears more likely for the Red Devils target

View 2 Images Orlando Gill is on the move after an impressive World Cup with Paraguay (Image: Anadolu, Anadolu via Getty Images)

World Cup star Orlando Gill was the subject of an enquiry from Manchester United, according to the player's representative, Mario Jara. The goalkeeper impressed for Paraguay as the South American nation faced the likes of France and upset Germany during the tournament.

‌



Gill is set to leave San Lorenzo this summer following his exploits, and United were among the candidates linked with his signature. Now, Jara has confirmed that the Red Devils reached out, though they no longer appear to be in the running.

‌



Senne Lammens established himself as United's first-choice keeper last season, and Michael Carrick has added Karl Darlow to his options from Leeds United. The former Newcastle shotstopper's arrival means it's unlikely another goalkeeper will arrive this summer.

‌



Nevertheless, Jara has confirmed he has held discussions with clubs in both England and Germany. The agent has indicated that the Gill is set to move imminently.

He told DSports Radio: "We are in talks with English clubs as well as clubs in Germany. There were enquiries with Manchester United.

Marcus Rashford posts Barcelona farewell message as dream return goes up in smoke READ MORE :

Man Utd ready to offload quartet including player they refused to swap for Carlos Baleba READ MORE :

"We only received two concrete offers. We are currently in the negotiation phase.

‌



"The sale is close, the time is right. We have to handle it very carefully because there are many things involved. It's ideal for him to take a step up in quality. He's prepared and capable of playing in any league, without a doubt."

He added: "We're trying to finalise it as quickly as possible for everyone's benefit. It would be very important for San Lorenzo; hopefully, it will come to fruition."

View 2 Images Orlando Gill was linked with a move to Manchester United this summer (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

United are more likely to see goalkeepers leave the club. Andre Onana has already departed on loan to Trabzonspor, while Altay Bayindir and Radek Vitek could both find new sides.

Vitek has featured in each of the Red Devils' friendlies so far, against Wrexham and Rosenborg, with Lammens only arriving back to Carrington on Thursday. Former Bristol City loanee is determined to find first-team action.

‌



"I feel great and ready to go again somewhere to be, hopefully, number one, so we will see. We will see what is going to happen," Vitek said after facing Wrexham.

"At the moment, I am still here, but we will see. I hope so. I hope there will be some interest. I think you will know when things are more concrete.

"I am ready for both, to be fair. [It] Depends what the club wants and also depends on the options. We will see.

"There have been a few interests on the table. But we hope to get the best one and hopefully it will happen soon."

Sports.title: 'Gianni Infantino should resign from FIFA now — or football will suffer forever'
Sports.content:
'Gianni Infantino should resign from FIFA now — or football will suffer forever'

Gianni Infantino, the president of FIFA since 2016, was on Thursday accused of "putting profit ahead of fans" amid the controversial plans to sell stakes of the World Cup

View Image Voice of the Mirror has its say...

FIFA boss Gianni Infantino has become a danger to the game he was elected to protect. His proposal to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors would reduce football’s greatest tournament to a financial asset, carved up by people interested in profit rather than passion. England will not take part. Neither will France, Germany, Spain, Italy or Europe’s other leading nations. They are right to threaten a boycott and must stand firm. Without Europe, the World Cup would be a sham: a gutted tournament missing many of its greatest teams, rivalries and supporters. Infantino knows this, yet he has still offered national associations £30 million to back his scheme. That is no way to run world football. It is an attempt to buy compliance while selling off the game’s crown jewels. The Mirror says Infantino has forfeited the right to lead FIFA. He should resign now. If he will not, he must be removed before his greed leaves football permanently poorer.

‌



Fires no freak

For weeks, Britain has watched in horror as wildfires tore through Europe. Now our own countryside is alight. More than 100 firefighters are battling flames across Suffolk heathland covering an area the size of 140 football pitches, while families have been forced from caravans and holiday parks. Their courage is extraordinary, as is the kindness of neighbours opening their homes to evacuees and their pets. Yet this cannot be dismissed as a freak disaster. We are heating the planet, drying the land and creating the conditions in which fires spread faster and burn harder. Andy Burnham must give crews every resource they need. But, despite the deniers, we all must act on the climate crisis with the urgency it demands. Europe’s nightmare is reaching our shores. Without change, this terrifying summer will become the new normal.

Ace in the old

At 100, Ivor Parker has finally turned a lifelong poker hobby into a job. After 86 years at the tables, he has been signed as the world’s oldest paid professional. His secret is patience, nerve and knowing when to hold ’em. Retirement, clearly, was never really on the cards.

Sports.title: Arne Slot immediately lined up for new job after Eddie Howe's bombshell Newcastle exit
Sports.content:
Arne Slot immediately lined up for new job after Eddie Howe's bombshell Newcastle exit

Arne Slot remains unemployed following his exit from Liverpool, but the Dutchman is now reportedly in the frame for a new job after developments involving Eddie Howe

View 2 Images Arne Slot is one of the contenders for the Al-Ahli job (Image: Getty Images)

Arne Slot could benefit from Eddie Howe's departure at Newcastle after the former Liverpool boss was reportedly shortlisted for the Al-Ahli job.

‌



Howe has walked away from Newcastle after five years in charge and the Magpies have already lined up his replacement. Newcastle have identified Al-Ahli manager Matthias Jaissle as the man to step into Howe's shoes on Tyneside ahead of the 2026/27 season.

‌



The club have been working on a succession plan for the past few weeks, with discontent growing behind the scenes. And the fact they are owned by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund - who also own Al-Ahli - has seen Jaissle in position to move to the Premier League.

‌



Slot has been in talks to succeed Ronald Koeman as the next Netherlands boss. But he could move to Saudi Arabia instead, with talkSPORT reporting that Slot is a candidate to replace Jaissle at Al-Ahli.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Chelsea, Sunderland and Nottingham Forest caught out as Premier League gambling ban bites READ MORE :

Five moments that defined Eddie Howe's rise and fall during Newcastle tenure READ MORE :

Slot was sacked by Liverpool in May following the conclusion of a disappointing season campaign at the club. He was approached by Fulham over succeeding Marco Silva, but rejected the opportunity, with Alvaro Arbeloa eventually taking the job instead.

‌



Former Wolves and Nottingham Forest boss Vitor Pereira is also a contender for the Al-Ahli role. He has experience in Saudi Arabia, having spent 10 months at Al Shabab, while he also previously managed Al Ahli in 2013.

The 58-year-old is available following a brief spell at Forest, where he lasted just 20 games and was replaced by ex-Crystal Palace boss Oliver Glasner this summer.

Whoever does take the job will have big shoes to fill, with Jaissle having won 92 of his 138 games in charge and won back-to-back Asian Champions League titles.

‌



View 2 Images Matthias Jaissle is leaving Al-Ahli for Newcastle (Image: FC Red Bull Salzburg via Getty Images)

Slot emerged as the main contender to replace Koeman after the World Cup. However, talks with the KNVB have stalled over the terms with Slot reportedly keen to only sign a deal until the end of the 2028 Euros, rather than until 2030.

If he does take the Netherlands job, then Slot would be following in the footsteps of his predecessor at Liverpool, Jurgen Klopp, who has taken the Germany role. Like the Netherlands, Germany changed head coach following a disappointing campaign at the World Cup.

Article continues below

Slot has been succeeded by Andoni Iraola at Liverpool, with the Spaniard having stepped up after three impressive campaigns at Bournemouth.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
