World.title: Berlin Pride attack: Are German juvenile courts too lenient?
World.content:
The terror attack on Berlin Pride has put the work of juvenile courts into the spotlight. Many argue the 21-year-old perpetrator should have been in prison at the time of the attack.

Could the terrorist attack on Berlin's Pride celebrations, allegedly by a 21-year-old Islamist, have been prevented? This question has been the subject of debate driven largely by the fact that the young German man — born in Germany in 2005 to parents of Lebanese origin — had been convicted and released just weeks before the attack.

Abdul Ballout, who drove his car into a crowd in Berlin's Tiergarten park — killing one woman and injuring 31 people, some seriously — had set out last year intending to join the so-called "Islamic State" (IS) terrorist group in Syria. However, he was arrested en route in Lebanon, detained there and subsequently deported to Germany.

Back in Germany, he stood trial on charges of preparing a serious act of violence endangering the state. He was found guilty and sentenced in mid-May to 22 months in prison, but this sentence was initially suspended. He was released — and attacked Berlin Pride just weeks later. The day after the incident, he was shot dead by police while they were attempting to arrest him.

Police 'should have kept an eye on' Berlin Pride attacker To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Juvenile sentencing can be applied to up to 20-year-olds because the brain is still developing at that age

Since then, juvenile criminal law in Germany has been the focus of criticism. Terrorism expert Peter Neumann from King's College London told the news portal T-Online: "This is a real problem. The sentences are too lenient. In my view, juvenile criminal law is sometimes interpreted too broadly. The protection of the public is not given sufficient consideration."

Juvenile criminal law serves special purposes, says Frieder Dünkel, a criminologist and criminal law expert from Greifswald. "It's primarily about education, about the reintegration of the young person," he told DW.

Judges have considerable leeway and can hand out admonitions or prison sentences.

In Germany, a perpetrator is criminally responsible from age 14 and juvenile criminal law applies. From the age of 18, regular criminal law generally applies, with higher minimum sentences. But juvenile criminal law can also be applied to young adults aged 18 to 20 if they show "developmental delays."

"This is because overall, one can still recognize significant developmental potential in 18- to 20-year-olds," Dünkel said.

This is backed by neuroscientific findings, according to Dünkel, showing that the brain areas responsible for behavioral control do not fully develop until the middle of the third decade of life. This implies that a young offender can still change for the better.

In May, Abdul Ballout was sentenced by the Berlin court under juvenile criminal law, even though he was already 21 at the time of his sentencing. However, he was only 20 years old when he committed the crimes he was found guilty of.

Berlin attack: When deradicalization programs don't work To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

'Preliminary probation' for Ballout

Ballout was able to leave the courthouse because he had been granted six months of "preliminary probation," after which the court would have had to make a final decision on whether he needed to go to prison. He was initially placed under intermittent police surveillance until the police officers concluded that he was behaving unobtrusively.

He was ordered to participate in an exit program for extremists, where he attended two preliminary meetings to determine whether he was indeed willing to critically examine his behavior and distance himself from extremism.

Preliminary probation is a relatively new concept in Germany's criminal law and was introduced in 2012. Frieder Dünkel believes that the mechanism has been successful in many cases.

"Specifically, when a juvenile court judge is unsure whether a sentence can or should be suspended in favor of probation, the judge orders a period of up to six months during which the young person is guided toward a law-abiding lifestyle through strict directives and monitoring measures," Dünkel explained.

German interior minister wants to reform juvenile criminal law

In the aftermath of the Berlin Pride attack, there have been calls to stop applying the more lenient juvenile criminal law to Islamist or right-wing extremist perpetrators.

But criminologist Dünkel disagrees: "It is not the role of juvenile criminal law to provide preventive protection for society before a crime has even been committed. Juvenile criminal law responds to crimes once they have been committed," he says.

Juvenile criminal law does allow for severe penalties; for instance, a murder conviction can result in a 15-year prison sentence for offenders aged 18 to 20.

Dünkel adds that recidivism rates among perpetrators sentenced under juvenile criminal law are no higher than among those sentenced under adult criminal law.

"Harsher penalties do not lead to greater security," he said.

Nevertheless, Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt of the conservative Christian Social Union (CSU) has announced his intention to examine ways to reform juvenile criminal law.

Konstantin von Notz, the opposition Green Party's expert on internal affairs disagrees with that approach.

"We... note that virtually all experts consulted on this matter so far point out that long prison sentences — especially for young adults — can have a counterproductive effect and may even accelerate existing radicalization," von Notz said.

What does the Berlin Pride attack mean for city's identity? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Information sharing glitch

Ballout had been classified as a dangerous individual by Germany's Joint Counter-Terrorism Center (GTAZ). The GTAZ is a coordination and communication platform established in 2004, after the 9/11 terror attacks in the United States, to combat Islamist terrorism through inter-agency information sharing.

However, the assessment of Ballout did not reach the Berlin court that handed down the lenient sentence earlier this year. If the information had been shared, Ballout may have remained incarcerated.

This article has been translated from German.

World.title: Epstein files: How victims remain exposed to identification
World.content:
US officials vowed to revise redactions after files exposed information that identified survivors of sexual abuse by Jeffrey Epstein and his associates. A DW investigation found that sensitive information remains online.

"I cannot live without looking over my shoulder," a sexual abuse survivor told US lawmakers in May, describing how her personal information was publicly exposed in January, when the Department of Justice (DOJ) released hundreds of thousands of documents related to the financier Jeffrey Epstein. "I can only imagine the long-term impact this mistake will have on my life."

Three days after the DOJ released the largest of 12 datasets on Epstein on January 30, a department lawyer told a federal court that "human or technical error" had been among the factors that led to the publishing of personally identifying information of people who had been sexually abused by Epstein and his associates. As a result, the DOJ said it would remove, review and redact flagged documents before republishing them.

DW's investigative unit, along with its Innovation and Data teams, spent months reviewing thousands of documents released by the DOJ. In the six months since the release, DW identified dozens of files that still contained information — including names, faces and email addresses — that could be used to identify survivors, witnesses and informants, among other people.

DOJ Epstein Library

By mid-February, DW had scraped more than 800,000 files from the DOJ's Epstein Library — a challenging task with the archive constantly changing: New files were being added, others were taken down and modified files were popping up after days of absence.

But it wasn't until DW obtained an earlier set of files archived by a publicly facing data preservation project on GitHub that we realized more than 500,000 files were removed between the initial days of the release and our scrape.

To verify the contents of the original release, DW generated a unique digital fingerprint, known as a hash, for every document. Hashes confirm that a document matches the original and hasn't been altered. By comparing these fingerprints with documents scraped from the DOJ website about two weeks later, DW could determine which files matched, as well as identify documents that had been removed from the DOJ website.

DW also found that some files had changed because the digital fingerprint was no longer the same: They had the same file name but were larger or smaller than the original. When DW reviewed this subset, we found that they represented files that had been further redacted — or information was added.

In one instance, a survivor described how Epstein had abused her for years as a minor in her testimony to lawyers. Her name was redacted throughout the transcript until the last page, when a lawyer thanked her for her testimony and said her name, and it remains unredacted as of publication.

Her exposed name was not an isolated case.

US lawmakers created strict rules on how the Epstein files should be published, such as ensuring that personally identifying information of victims be redacted to protect them from public exposure Image: picture-alliance/dpa/M. Reynolds

Deep audio analysis

To analyze audio files, including victim statements and tipoffs, DW's investigative unit collaborated with the Fraunhofer Institute for Digital Media Technology's Media Distribution and Security research group in Ilmenau, Germany. The MDS specializes in audio authenticity, manipulation and speech synthesis detection.

After removing duplicated files from the publicly facing data preservation project and DW's scrape, we were left with more than 150 audio files, which the MDS's forensic audio researchers analyzed using state-of-the-art tools developed at the institute. They detected digital traces left by audio production and editing processes that are, at times, inaudible to the human ear.

That included identifying parts of a recording that had been modified or reused, determining whether a recording was an altered version of another file, and assessing whether audio files may have been recorded using the same microphone or recording setup.

Forensic audio researcher Milica Gerhardt observed something unique: that redaction styles varied across the files, along with inconsistencies in how redactions were executed.

"If one observes the content of these audio files, one can see that a lot of personal information has not been redacted," Gerhardt said.

Using the Audio Provenance Suite App, Gerhardt identified two files in the same dataset with identical content, but one was redacted and the other unredacted Image: Stefan Czimmek/DW

In one case, a person called an official tipoff hotline to report information for use in an investigation into Epstein's abuse. In the redacted version, you can hear the person's name, but their phone number was bleeped out.

The same dataset, however, also contained a different version of the audio file, in which the person's full name could be heard as well as their direct contact. Alleged witnesses or informants were apparently not included in the protections allotted to victims.

"They could and should have done a better job on the redactions," said Patrick Aichroth, who heads the MDS group at the Fraunhofer Institute, which has consulted on audio-related evidence for judicial authorities in Germany.

"There is a reason why such material is treated so carefully in court cases," Aichroth said. "Once sensitive or identifying information is disclosed, the damage cannot be undone."

Redactions across audio files were inconsistent and revealed sensitive information, according to audio forensics researchers. Image: Stefan Czimmek/DW

DOJ's redaction failures

DW's investigative unit confronted the DOJ with its findings, including examples in which survivors' personally identifiable information remained in the official Epstein Library.

The DOJ did not respond.

In April, the DOJ's Office of the Inspector General, an independent watchdog tasked with investigating misconduct within the department, announced that it was "initiating an audit of DOJ's compliance with the Epstein Files Transparency Act."

"Our preliminary objective is to evaluate the DOJ's processes for identifying, redacting and releasing records in its possession as required by the Act," the office said in a statement.

In July, several lawmakers introduced the Epstein Files Transparency Act II, which would allow sexual abuse survivors and the governments of US states to take the DOJ to court for failing to comply with the rules laid out in the initial Transparency Act, which had guaranteed that the personally identifiable information of survivors would be protected.

Survivors whose information was published unredacted have since shared accounts of harassment, humiliation and physical threats. With the publicly disclosed information still available on public platforms and, in some cases, still on the DOJ website, the impact continues to upend survivors' lives.

"While the rich and powerful remain protected by redactions, my name was exposed to the world," said the sexual abuse survivor who gave her testimony to Congress in May.

"The evidence is right here," she said, "yet those in power [would] rather us die socially, emotionally and physically than admit their own complicity."

Edited by: Mathias Bölinger, Milan Gagnon

Technical and data analysis by: Andreas Giefer

Data journalists: Gianna Grün, Rodrigo Menegat Schuinski

Fact checking by: Birgitta Schülke

World.title: UEFA votes to boycott World Cup over FIFA investor plan
World.content:
UEFA members unanimously voted to boycott ‌the ⁠World ⁠Cup and other competitions unless FIFA abandons its private investor plans. "The World Cup is not for sale," they said, as FIFA seeks to sell a stake in it.

European football's governing body, UEFA, voted unanimously to boycott FIFA competitions if the world governing body proceeds with plans to create a new commercial subsidiary valued at $20 billion (roughly €17.5 billion) and sell a non-controlling minority stake in it to investors.

The subsidiary would be responsible for FIFA's commercial rights like broadcast, sponsorship, ticketing and licensing contracts for its competitions, including the World Cup.

UEFA's 55 members met to discuss a response to FIFA President Gianni Infantino's controversial plans.

"No UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership," UEFA said in a statement.

"The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product... No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale," the statement added.

Shortly after, North America’s soccer body CONCACAF unanimously rejected the FIFA plan, though it stopped short of a boycott.

UEFA swiftly rejected FIFA's proposal

UEFA had come out publicly in opposition to the plan within an hour of it first being reported by the Financial Times and Times on Tuesday.

Shortly after the newspaper reports, FIFA, the sport's global governing body, issued a statement confirming the plan.

In a later statement, it gave FIFA's 211 member associations until September 19 to express their written support for the scheme. The proposal requires a simple majority and approval from the FIFA Council to pass.

Even before Thursday's meeting, UEFA had doubled down on its criticism after learning of the deadline, saying: "Today we have learned of FIFA's deadline to associations to support their proposals or have the one-off payout offer withdrawn. This says everything ​you need to know about this plan.

Aleksander Ceferin's UEFA has been at loggerheads with FIFA for some time Image: Mike Egerton/PA/picture alliance

It added that talks with many stakeholders showed that "there is significant and growing opposition to FIFA's scheme. FIFA cannot to use our sport to enrich themselves and their friends."

DFB: FIFA plan 'problematic and unacceptable'

Germany's mass-circulation Bild paper reported that key UEFA officials including German FA (DFB) President Bernd Neuendorf had already discussed the FIFA plans via a video call on Wednesday.

"We must not lose the fans' support, but we are well on the way to squandering that," he told public broadcaster ZDF. "I consider this to be extremely problematic and unacceptable.

"If UEFA rejects this request (for approval of the plan), then it is dead, because I believe that you won't be able to find any investor who would be willing to go ahead with this project if UEFA is out," he added.

Bernd Neuendorf can't see the FIFA plan going forward without UEFA on board Image: Ulrich Wagner/picture alliance

Other critics have expressed fears that the deal could lead to more tournaments, teams and matches to increase revenue and boost the value of investors' stakes.

UEFA hasn't been the only confederation to criticize the report. CONCACAF, responsible for North and Central America, as well as the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) have also expressed concerns that the proposal was made public without their consultation while the African confederation (CAF) have said they will discuss the plans next week.

Members of the FIFA Council, including Neuendorf, have said they were not consulted on the latest proposal.

FIFA: Subsidiary could raise billions 'this year'

FIFA has said the new subsidiary, to be known as FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) would be valued at $20 billion and that it would aim to raise up to $4.2 billion "this year" by "carefully selecting long-term investors who will purchase minority, non-controlling interests" in the company.

Under the ​plan, FIFA said it could make $10 billion available for development beginning in 2027. Each federation would be eligible for up to $20 ​million in one-time Fast Forward funding, in addition to $20 million through the regular FIFA Forward program during the 2027-30 ⁠cycle. Without ​approval, FIFA projects a development package of about $2.7 billion.

FIFA unveils controversial World Cup investor plan To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Infantino: 'A golden opportunity'

In the face of the opposition, FIFA President Gianni Infantino released a video on Wednesday evening, describing the project a "golden opportunity to turbocharge the development of the game globally."

He added that the proposal was "part of a democratic process" and in comments directed to football fans, he stressed that "the sport they watch and love will not change."

Edited by: Matt Pearson

World.title: Última hora de la entrada de inmigrantes a Ceuta, en directo | Ceuta amanece con cientos de jóvenes durmiendo en la calle mientras continúa el cruce de personas por la frontera
World.content:
El PP pide cambiar la Ley de Extranjería para garantizar "el rechazo en frontera" y la comparecencia urgente de Sánchez en un pleno extraordinario en el Congreso

El PP acaba de emitir un comunicado en el que pide, entre otras cuestiones, cambiar la Ley de Extranjería “para garantizar que la figura del rechazo en frontera aplique también a las entradas por vía marítima a las ciudades de Ceuta y Melilla, en los términos de la proposición de ley que registró el Partido Popular el día 16 de julio. También solicitan que la Diputación permanente del Congreso se reúna para convocar un pleno extraordinario centrado en la crisis de Ceuta y se sustancie en ese foro la comparecencia urgente del presidente del Gobierno. La formación de Alberto Núñez Feijóo insiste además en solicitar la declaración de Ceuta como situación de interés para la seguridad nacional y el ”despliegue de medios masivos“. ”A Ceuta ha seguido llegando gente toda la noche y quienes están sobre el terreno describen una ciudad ocupada, sin que se esté haciendo nada suficiente para evitarlo. En Melilla también han entrado unos 400 irregulares“, añade Feijóo a través de un mensaje en redes sociales. ”Insisto en que Pedro Sánchez tiene que defender nuestra seguridad nacional, nuestra integridad territorial y nuestra convivencia. Como presidente del Gobierno tiene instrumentos y medios a su disposición, y solo resta que dé las órdenes. Tan grave como lo que está pasando es que el Gobierno reaccione con esta debilidad. Toda España está con Ceuta y Melilla", añade el líder del PP.

World.title: El Santander lanza una oferta por el 10% de su filial en Brasil que no controla por 1.900 millones y una prima del 15%
World.content:
El Banco Santander ha anunciado una oferta para tomar el control total de su filial en Brasil. La entidad que preside Ana Botín quiere hacerse con todo el capital de Santander Brasil que aún no posee, aproximadamente un 10%, mediante un canje de acciones de nueva emisión, con un importe máximo de 1.908 millones de euros, lo que implica una prima del 15% respecto a su última cotización.

La contraprestación ofrecida consistirá en 0,4056 acciones de nueva emisión de Banco Santander por cada unit o American Depositary Shares (ADS) de Santander Brasil y 0,2028 acciones del Santander por cada acción ordinaria o preferente de Santander Brasil, según notificó el banco a la Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores (CNMV) en un hecho relevante. De esta forma, el Santander trata de aprovechar la menor valoración de su filial brasileña para intentar de nuevo hacerse con todo el capital.

Ya desde principios del año pasado comenzaron a circular especulaciones en el mercado sobre una posible oferta pública de adquisición sobre la filial brasileña, dado que la valoración de las acciones de Brasil se quedó rezagada con respecto a la de la matriz, debido a los crecientes problemas de crédito en la mayor economía de Latinoamérica. En los últimos meses, a medida que la cotización de la matriz del Santander ha ido tomando vuelo, la brecha no ha hecho más que ampliarse y la entidad que preside Ana Botín se ha convertido en el banco más valioso de Europa.

La oferta supone una prima del 15% respecto al precio de referencia de cada acción de Santander Brasil. Según cálculos de la entidad, en caso de que todos los accionistas minoritarios acudieran a la oferta, el Santander emitiría aproximadamente 156 millones de nuevas acciones, equivalentes a aproximadamente el 1,1% de su capital social actual, y la operación tendrá un importe máximo 1.908 millones de euros. La entrega de acciones nuevas se realizará, según corresponda, en forma de Brazilian Depositary Receipts (BDR) o de ADS, que cotizarán en la Bolsa de São Paulo y en la Bolsa de Nueva York, respectivamente. La operación se llevará a cabo mediante ofertas públicas de canje voluntarias y simultáneas en Brasil y Estados Unidos.

Aunque la oferta se extiende la totalidad de las acciones en circulación de Santander Brasil, la entidad asegura que no busca excluir de la bolsa a la filial brasileña y que la oferta es voluntaria, pero en función de los resultados, las acciones sí podrían dejar de cotizar en la Bolsa de Nueva York y cancelarse su registro ante la Comisión de Bolsa y Valores de Estados Unidos (SEC).

La ampliación de capital necesaria para la operación se someterá a la aprobación de la junta general de accionistas. El banco destacó que esta operación “refleja la confianza de Banco Santander en Brasil y en el potencial de crecimiento de su negocio en el país”.

En un comunicado, la entidad señaló que la oferta es “una alternativa atractiva” frente a otras opciones de asignación de capital y tiene un impacto neutro sobre la ratio de capital del grupo. Se espera que contribuya a aumentar el beneficio por acción en aproximadamente un 0,5% a partir de 2028 y el valor contable tangible por acción en aproximadamente un 0,6%. También contribuirá a reforzar el crecimiento del beneficio del grupo a largo plazo y su capacidad de generación orgánica de capital.

Para los accionistas minoritarios de Santander Brasil, la entidad destacó que es una “atractiva oportunidad para materializar el valor de su inversión con una prima significativa sobre el precio de mercado” y les permitirá ser accionistas de uno de los principales grupos financieros del mundo.

La presidenta del Santander, Ana Botín, afirmó que esta operación “supone un paso más en nuestra estrategia de simplificar el grupo, al tiempo que reforzamos nuestro compromiso a largo plazo con Brasil”, declaró la presidenta quien se comprometió a “seguir reforzando nuestra apuesta por Brasil a largo plazo”.

La filial brasileña es uno de las áreas más importantes de Santander, que ocupó el primer lugar en ingresos durante el primer semestre de este año, según datos de Bloomberg. Sin embargo, la rentabilidad disminuyó en los últimos años debido a que las altas tasas de interés afectaron el modelo de negocio, que depende de la financiación al consumo.

Para los analistas, la caída de las acciones y la depreciación del real brasileño explican la decisión, además del capital flotante relativamente pequeño, afirmó a Bloomberg Fernando Siqueira, jefe de investigación de Eleven Financial. “Por otro lado, también parece indicar confianza en que los débiles resultados de los últimos trimestres son solo temporales”, señaló.

Además, se han producido varios cambios recientes en la dirección brasiñela. El consejero delegado, Mario Leão, dejó la compañía este mes y fue reemplazado por Gilson Finkelsztain. A principios de año, Gustavo Alejo renunció a su cargo de director financiero y fue sucedido por Carlos Muñiz.

Las acciones de Santander Brasil registraron este miércoles su mayor caída en más de seis años, tras la publicación de resultados del segundo trimestre que no alcanzaron las previsiones de los analistas debido al fuerte aumento de los costes crediticios. Muñiz afirmó que Santander está reduciendo su exposición a productos de mayor riesgo y que no prevé que el panorama macroeconómico cambie antes del próximo año.

World.title: Mi casero quiere recuperar la vivienda para uso propio tras 17 años, pero en el contrato no figura esta cláusula, ¿puede hacerlo?
World.content:
Pregunta. He estado viviendo en una casa en un pueblo de la provincia de Toledo durante 17 años sin deber ningún alquiler y ahora el propietario me ha enviado un burofax pidiéndome que deje la vivienda porque la necesita para su uso personal. Esta cláusula no está en el contrato de arrendamiento de vivienda firmado en 2009. ¿Cuáles son mis derechos como inquilino? Goyo.

Respuesta. Si en su contrato de alquiler no está prevista la posibilidad de que se le pueda poner fin al mismo por causa de necesidad del arrendador para que sea habitada por él, el propietario no puede poner fin al contrato por este motivo. Sin embargo, teniendo en cuenta que su contrato es del año 2009, a no ser que la duración pactada hubiera sido por más de los 17 años que ya lleva vigente, el contrato se encuentra actualmente en situación de prórroga legal.

En esta fase, la duración de la prórroga depende de la forma en que se haya establecido la renta en el contrato: el contrato se prórroga por meses, si la renta pactada en el contrato es mensual; o se prórroga anualmente, si en el contrato se pactó una renta anual (aunque se pague mensualmente).

De modo que cada vez que se produzca el vencimiento del periodo de prórroga correspondiente, mensual, en el primer caso, o anual, en el segundo caso, el propietario podría poner fin al contrato. Para ello, bastaría con que comunique la decisión dejando constancia de su recepción con una antelación mínima de un mes respecto de la fecha en que vaya a producirse la siguiente renovación, mensual o anual, en función de lo anteriormente comentado.

Si tiene dudas, sugerencias o simplemente quiere contarnos su caso, puede enviarnos un email a vivienda@elpais.es .

World.title: Rosa Vañó (Castillo de Canena): “Madonna es una de las personas más complicadas y con más ego con las que he trabajado”
World.content:
Economista de formación, dejó su exitosa carrera de directiva en Coca-Cola para desarrollar, junto a su hermano Francisco, la explotación olivarera que había creado su padre en Jaén. Además, conoce muy bien el mundo de las discográficas ya que trabajó para Warner Music y Universal

Es la gran dama del aceite español. Rosa Vañó (Madrid, 63 años), economista de formación, abandonó una exitosa carrera como directiva de Coca-Cola, donde se dedicaba al desarrollo de nuevas líneas de negocio, lanzamientos y reposicionamiento de productos, para dedicarse, junto a su hermano Francisco, al sueño que inició su padre, Luis Vañó: impulsar Castillo de Canena, una explotación olivarera con almazara situada en Canena (Jaén), propiedad de su familia y reconocida con numerosos premios nacionales e internacionales. Anteriormente trabajó en las discográficas Warner Music y Universal, “donde aprendí a gestionar egos y a entender que hay que contar con los medios de comunicación como embajadores y transmisores de la creatividad y el valor añadido de los músicos”. Ejerce también como tesorera de la Real Academia de Gastronomía.

Pregunta. Con este bagaje, decide desarrollar su propio negocio.

Respuesta. Sí, porque teníamos la enorme suerte de tener campo, almazara y también el castillo. Se puede empezar de cero, pero de distintas formas. Es un recorrido profesional que te va formando y quitando miedos. La ignorancia es muy valiente y te hace creer que puedes hacer las cosas mejor, de forma diferente y de manera especial. Todo esto cuesta mucho trabajo. Primero, porque no es fácil hacerlo y porque hay mucha gente que lo hace igual o mejor que tú. Al final, la fórmula no es otra que trabajo, pero bien entendido.

P. ¿Qué significa esto?

R. El trabajo no son horas, es calidad y flexibilidad. Los peores resultados los he tenido cuando he trabajado 14 horas al día. He sido menos resolutiva y creativa. Me parece importante la conectividad para mi conciliación como madre, como hija y como profesional. Son las tres prioridades de mi vida. El teléfono me permite tener mi sitio de trabajo en cualquier lugar.

P. Comentaba que sabe manejar los egos. ¿Se ha encontrado con muchos?

R. Madonna es una de las personas más complicadas y con más ego que he conocido y con la que he trabajado en mi vida. Me tocó trabajar con ella en promoción y en gira. Por el contrario, con Phil Collins o los hermanos Young [Malcolm y Angus], de AC/DC, me he divertido mucho. Son personas que han dejado el ego a un lado. Y no tiene nada que ver con que sean hombres o mujeres. Por ejemplo, Prince era un hombre que tenía inseguridades, pero con una gestión muy peculiar de su ego. Porque el ego no es solo el de tipo Madonna, en el que tienes que interpretar su gestión, sino también cómo se siente, cómo es su timidez y cómo tienes que relacionarte con él. Seal tampoco era una persona fácil. Fue mi primer artista y era complicado de manejar.

P. ¿Qué se hace en esos casos?

R. Callar, entender y destensar la situación, aunque no tengas la culpa. Hay que intentar destensar y tratar de ser empático y resolutivo. El ego es más complejo que creerse superior, por eso hay que entender cómo es la personalidad de cada uno. Ha sido una gran escuela de vida.

P. Salir a vender aceite por el mundo habrá sido mucho más fácil, ¿no?

R. La primera vez que salí a vender aceite fue en España. Entré en un restaurante, que no voy a decir cuál, por la puerta principal. Me preguntaron a qué iba y les dije que a vender aceite. Me dijeron que eso era por la puerta de proveedores, que estaba por detrás, donde estaban los cubos de basura y los cascos de botellas. Entré por ahí. Hoy, si no me dicen lo contrario, siempre entro por la puerta de proveedores. Entiendo que, si el cocinero me tiene que recibir en su cocina para probar el aceite, esa es la puerta. Hay que entender cada situación.

P. ¿Ha hecho mucha calle?

R. Al principio hay que hacer mucha calle. Ahora también, pero tenemos más gente que te ayuda. Estoy en un momento de mi vida en el que tengo que mirarlo todo con mucha positividad. Lo mejor es hoy y tengo que estar preparada para el día de mañana. Debe haber un relevo. Hay decisiones que ya no me toca tomar a mí, sino al equipo, a mi sobrino y a mi hijo [ambos se llaman Luis y llevan el apellido Vañó]. Me pueden pedir opinión, pero no puedo empecinarme en que la decisión es mía porque hay gente alrededor que tiene que liderar. Odiaría ser la típica persona que es la primera que llega a la oficina y la última que se va. O la que va todos los días, con 80 años, a ver qué pasa.

P. ¿A qué dedica el resto del tiempo cuando no trabaja?

R. Voy a ir por orden de frivolidad. Me gusta jugar al golf; hago pilates tres días a la semana, que me divierte mucho, y camino. Soy una gran aficionada a viajar, pero con causa. Mi afición siempre ha sido la antropología, la arqueología y el arte antiguo. Me ha interesado saber cuándo el hombre deja de ser animal y adquiere un toque divino o humano. Me gusta viajar con contenido, por ejemplo, para ver el románico del norte de España, el misterio de las catedrales, conocer culturas antiguas... Es algo que no he hecho en los últimos años todo lo que me habría gustado y me gustaría retomarlo. Coger un barco y recorrer las esclusas francesas, pararte en los vignerons y vas viendo el paisaje, me gusta. Me voy a dedicar a viajar más. También he descuidado mucho mi afición a las exposiciones. Antes iba prácticamente todos los meses a ver dos exposiciones en Madrid y, si tenía que irme fuera, también lo hacía. Pero ahora, por mi situación personal, he descuidado un poco esa faceta. Me encantaba ir con toda la familia a ver una exposición y luego irnos a comer. Me parece gratificante. Adoro leer.

P. ¿Cuál es su género preferido?

R. Leo mucha historia, pero como formo parte de varias tertulias literarias me hacen leer todo tipo de libros. Uno de los más recientes ha sido Historia de una escalera. También acabo de leer varias obras de Hermann Hesse para una tertulia. Me esfuerzo por leer cosas diferentes de las que suelo leer durante el insomnio.

P. ¿Qué lee en esas noches en vela?

R. Leo a Agatha Christie y a sir Arthur Conan Doyle. Quiero lecturas ligeras para quedarme dormida. La ópera me ha encantado toda la vida. He estado en distintos teatros, como el Bolshói o La Scala de Milán. Verdi y Puccini me encantan porque mi madre me los ponía de pequeña. Voy a cuatro o cinco óperas al año. También me encanta la música barroca. No me pierdo los ciclos de Händel en el Auditorio Nacional de Música de Madrid.

P. ¿Qué restaurantes frecuenta?

R. Tanto de producto y muy clásicos como sorprendentes y de vanguardia. Me gustan los dos extremos. Estuve hace poco en Desde 1911 y trabaja con un gran producto. También me gustan las verduras de Saddle o el ganso de Navidad, que tomo con mis hijos. Los atunes guisados de El Campero me encantan. No me gustan los crudos. Estuve hace poco en Tetsu y me pareció espectacular y divertido. De Jaén me gustan Juan Carlos García, de Vandelvira, y Pedro Sánchez, de Bagá; también Dani Carnero, del restaurante Kaleja en Málaga. Son maravillosos. Y José Álvarez, en la costa de Almería, con su proyecto de tomates.

P. ¿Su desayuno preferido?

R. Una tostada de pan bien caliente, restregada con ajo, aceite de oliva virgen extra y sal. El ajo es maravilloso de todas las maneras. No soy muy cafetera, tomo uno al día. Me gusta su olor, pero no tanto el sabor.

P. ¿Le gusta darse caprichos?

R. No, salvo gastronómicos. Comprarme ropa siempre tiene que ser algo organizado. Hace años, una compañera de trabajo me dijo que salía con la misma ropa en todas las fotografías. Nunca se lo agradeceré lo suficiente porque no había caído en ello. Soy muy estructurada con lo que me pongo, pero ir de compras me aburre. También me aburren las obras en casa y comprar cosas para decorarla.

P. ¿Tiene algún viaje pendiente?

R. Cuando era pequeña leí los libros de Jack London y sus viajes a los mares del Sur. Por eso me atrae la Polinesia, aunque luego quizá sea un coñazo y tenga que llevarme 200 libros, preguntándome qué hago yo en un palafito. Me gustaría conocerla. También me gustaría ver una aurora boreal. La Antártida me resulta muy atractiva. Y me apetecería hacer un viaje en barco entre Moscú y San Petersburgo.

P. ¿Algún remedio para el insomnio?

R. La edad no perdona. He probado todo lo que no es químico y, a veces, funciona y otras no. Ya convivo con él, incluso cuando estoy de vacaciones en Granada, frente al mar Mediterráneo, al que tanto quiero. Lo que no me gusta es pensar por la noche porque es muy mala compañera. También escucho pódcasts ligeros y de true crime; eso me evade y evita que me invadan los malos pensamientos, porque soy una persona muy positiva y estable.

World.title: One person dies, six injured in crash between lorry and minibus
World.content:
One person has died and six others have been seriously injured in a head-on collision between a minibus and a lorry in Overijssel.

The crash happened on the N48 near Balkbrug, around 20km east of Zwolle, at around 11.30am on Thursday. All the victims were sitting in the minibus, which had Belgian numberplates.

Fire appliances, ambulances and an air ambulance were called to the crash site. Six passengers were taken to different hospitals in the area, while the seventh was pronounced dead at the scene. The lorry driver was unharmed.

The road is likely to be closed for several hours while police carry out investigations and the road is cleared of debris.

World.title: University launches ethics probe into Red Bull professor’s work
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Utrecht University has begun an investigation into its pharmacology department after a professor was accused of not declaring payments for research from companies, including energy drinks manufacturer Red Bull.

Joris Verster published several papers on energy drinks and alcohol in his capacity as associate professor, without disclosing that he was also paid as a consultant for Red Bull and US-based Sen-Jam Pharmaceuticals.

The university does not prohibit consultancy work, but academics are required to disclose any relevant secondary activities when they publish papers under conflict of interest rules.

The investigation follows reports in several Dutch and international media outlets, including Trouw, De Groene Amsterdammer and Investico, that Verster’s research was published without any reference to his paid work for Red Bull and Sen-Jam.

Verster set up a private company, NeuroClinics, for his consultancy work, which frequently overlapped with his academic research.

Hangover pill

He carried out a study into a hangover pill produced by Sen-Jam which concluded, based on a questionnaire circulated around his students, that the medicine did not encourage people to consume more alcohol.

Mariëtte van den Hoven, professor of medical ethics at Amsterdam’s UMC medical centre, said Verster’s methods amounted to a conflict of interest “by using the university to promote your personal goals.”

Another study, published in 2010, concluded that drinking a can of Red Bull improved driving performance, based on observing drivers for four hours in a simulator. It was publicised under the heading “Can Red Bull fuel better driving?”

Verster also published research that disputed claims that mixing energy drinks with alcohol were damaging to people’s health and could lead to aggressive behaviour or unsafe sexual practices.

His conclusion was that combining the drinks meant users consumed less alcohol and were less prone to reckless behaviour.

Sick leave

Verster himself, who has been on sick leave since the start of May, told Trouw he had always been transparent about his private work.

“I have been a consultant for many companies and stated it in all my papers, even when it concerned a minor role,” he said. “I informed Utrecht University about my work as a consultant and the university approved it.”

World.title: Eighth species of American crayfish found in Dutch rivers
World.content:
A new species of crayfish has been found in Dutch rivers, the eighth type to establish itself in the Netherlands after being introduced in the upper Rhine.

The calico crayfish (Faxonius immunis), originally from North America, was spotted in Gelderland by ecologist Pim Lemmers, who first encountered the creatures in a nature reserve near Karlsruhe decades ago.

“I’d been expecting them and looking out for them for a while,” he told NOS. “Last year I found a crayfish pincer and I knew straight away that it might be a significant one.“

The discovery of the pincer, together with the results of DNA samples, are enough to confirm that the crayfish have made it to the Dutch river system.

The water authority in Rivierland has reported the presence of the crayfish to the food standards regulator NVWA, which will in turn notify the European Union, and triggered the protocol for dealing with invasive exotic species.

The Dutch agriculture ministry has set up a working group to investigate how the crayfish can be prevented from spreading. Crayfish damage the local environment by eating indigenous plants and animals and digging in river banks.

“We’re at a very uncertain stage, because are they just in the Klompenwaard area of the Rhine or are they already in our regional waters? Can we keep them out of the waters?” said José Vos, senior policy adviser for the water board.

World.title: Post-Covid fatigue not just caused by inactivity, study finds
World.content:
Patients with post-Covid syndrome suffer muscle damage that cannot be fully be explained by inactivity, research led by scientists at Amsterdam’s Vrije Universiteit (VU) has found.

The team compared the blood and muscle tissue of patients with long Covid and chronic fatigue (ME) with a group of healthy people who spent 60 days in bed as part of a study simulating the effects of space travel.

The post-Covid and ME patients had suffered from energy dips that caused them to avoid exercising or spend long periods in bed, which has a degrading impact on the skeletal muscles.

But the researchers, led by Rob Wüst, a movement scientist at the VU, found differences in the colour of the muscle fibres between the two groups, indicating that the post-Covid patients had a much lower oxygen capacity.

“As skeletal muscle characteristics differ between patients and healthy individuals after bed rest, physical inactivity cannot solely explain the lower exercise capacity and skeletal muscle adaptations in long Covid and ME/CFS patients,” they wrote in a paper published in Nature Communications.

The healthy individuals from the space programme still had bright red fibres, which are still oxygen-rich, while the patients had white fibres, which become exhausted much faster.

Rapid tiredness

The researchers said the difference could explain why post-Covid and ME sufferers become tired so quickly even after modest levels of exercise or exertion. “The redder the fibres, the more stamina a person has,” Wüst explained.

Lung specialist Merel Hellemons, of the Erasmus MC teaching hospital in Rotterdam, told the Volkskrant that the findings were a crucial development in understanding how to treat patients with conditions such as post-Covid syndrome.

“Many patients hear that they need to move more or that being less active is bad for them,” she said.

Wüst said patients should still be encouraged to be more mobile to avoid damage to their muscles, skeletons and cardiovascular system caused by inactivity. “The question is: what is possible? We need more tailored solutions,” he said.

World.title: Profits at KLM up in 2026 despite fuel cost increases
World.content:

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Dutch airline KLM booked a higher-than-expected profit in the first half of the year, despite the rise in fuel prices caused by ongoing conflicts in the Middle East.

The company reported revenue of €6.9 bn in the six months to June, an 8% increase compared to the same period last year.

The airline benefited from a decrease in flights from competitors like Qatar Airways and Emirates because of the unrest in the region.

“The measures we are implementing are having a positive impact on our results,” CEO Marjan Rintel said in a statement.

Those measures included passing on higher fuel prices to customers, particularly on long-haul flights.

Yesterday, the Air France-KLM airline group announced they had put in an offer for a stake in Portugal’s TAP airline. Lisbon said last year that it was seeking a major international airline to buy most of the 49.9 percent stake that it planned to sell.

German airline Lufthansa also submitted a bid.

World.title: Man who strangled partner jailed after new forensic method used
World.content:
A man has been convicted of attempting to kill his partner in the first case to use new techniques to detect signs of strangulation in domestic violence.

The 33-year-old man from Rozenburg grabbed the woman by the neck as an argument turned violent last November. Police were alerted by neighbours and pulled the man away from his victim, who later said she was “turning blue”.

She was examined by a medical specialist using a new procedure developed in Rotterdam to gather forensic evidence faster in suspected cases of strangulation.

The doctor said the attack could have been fatal if it was prolonged, a detail that allowed prosecutors to argue that the attack should be classed as attempted manslaughter.

The procedure was introduced last December to try to detect strangulation, which is seen as an early warning sign of femicide, in domestic abuse investigations before the victim’s injuries heal and the evidence disappears.

200 referrals

The medical agency FARR, based in Rotterdam, anticipated receiving 200 inquiries a year, but was called on 150 times in the first three months. In 92% of cases doctors concluded the injuries could have been caused by strangulation. Nine in 10 victims were female and 78% of inquiries were related to domestic violence.

“It’s a huge number,” the agency’s managing director Geranda Zeelenberg told NOS. “Previously we hardly ever saw these people. They were probably always there, but the research we’ve begun has increased awareness of these cases.”

The man from Rozenburg was sentenced to 360 days in prison for attempted manslaughter, including 169 days suspended, and a community service order of 150 hours, in line with the prosecution’s demands.

His lawyer told the court he had no recollection of the events on the night of the attack because he had been taking alcohol and amphetamines, but argued that he had attacked her to try to force her to have sex rather than attempting to kill her.

World.title: Middle East conflict adds to pressure to fill Dutch gas reserves
World.content:
The Netherlands is lagging behind its European partners in filling its gas reserves for the winter, just as a key supplier in the Middle East has announced further restrictions on supplies caused by the conflict between the US and Iran.

QatarEnergy extended “force majeure” restrictions on its LNG cargoes until the end of September, affecting a total of 24 cargoes to European customers.

The company signed a contract to supply up to 3.5 million tonnes of liquified gas to the Netherlands per annum, which came into force this year, but the invocation of force majeure has put this commitment in jeopardy.

The Netherlands’ gas reserves are currently at 36.6% capacity, well below the EU average of 56%.

Following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, which triggered a spike in prices, the EU set a target of reaching 90% capacity by November 1. Since then European nations have had to find alternatives to Russian gas.

The Netherlands achieved this level for the first three years, but in 2025 it peaked at just 74% and at the start of April this year the four Dutch storage facilities were at less than 5% capacity.

Energy minister Stientje van Veldhoven said last month she was “confident” that the gas reserves would be filled for the winter, but admitted that the government needed to be “vigilant”.

Demand for gas has also increased during the summer as more consumer and businesses install air conditioning, putting more pressure on energy.

The Dutch government also has agreements to buy gas from Norway and the United States, or could resort to the open market.

The wholesale price of gas on the TTF market, operated by Gasunie, has risen by 50% since mid-June as a result of ongoing attacks by Iran and the US on facilities in the Middle East and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: Sitting targets: thieves make off with 88 museum cafe chairs
World.content:

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Thieves walked off with all of the chairs from the Bonnefanten Museum café in Maastricht in the early hours of Monday.

Café manager Freek Joosten told local news network L1 that camera footage showed the perpetrators making several trips carrying stacks of chairs at around 4am.

The designer seats are valued at more than €21,000.

The chairs were tied down with iron cables and the grounds are monitored by multiple cameras. The museum has reported the theft to the police.

The museum, which sits on Avenue Céramique in the Limburg capital, specialises in visual arts.

The terrace was recently renovated and the chairs were from designer Fermob Luxembourg. The thieves also took a waste container.

Visitors are still welcome in the café. Joosten has temporarily reallocated the chairs from his catering business to use on the terrace.

Police have asked anyone who saw anything unusual in the vicinity on the night of July 26 to 27, or who may have camera footage, to contact them.

Poland’s government has appointed a marketing and branding expert to develop a unified strategy for promoting the country abroad, saying the move will help boost tourism, support Polish products and attract foreign investment. Barbara Mróz-Gorgoń, a professor at Wrocław University of Economics, noted that her appointment signals “a shift” from simple promotional activities to “managing the reputation of our great country”. The move comes as Poland seeks to capitalise on its economic success, including growth in tourism and continued investments. But the government says that current promotion efforts lack a single strategy and are fragmented. Czas na markę Polska! Witamy na pokładzie prof. Barbarę Mróz – Gorgoń 🇵🇱 pic.twitter.com/PPX2eWTRSm — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) July 29, 2026 Last year, Poland’s sport and tourism ministry appointed Mróz-Gorgoń, who also advises companies and institutions on branding strategy and founded a think tank dedicated to promoting Poland, to an interministerial team tasked with developing a comprehensive new branding strategy for Poland. The government said, however, that efforts to promote Poland were so far fragmented and lacked a single strategy, which is why it created the post of commissioner for promotion of the Poland brand. As the first specialist to take the position, Mróz-Gorgoń will be tasked with preparing a strategy to build a national brand and help implement it, coordinate activities to help grow tourism, support investments, and improve Poland’s position on the world stage. “We will create one programme resulting in the joint promotion of our country’s brand,” said Tusk. According to the government, this will come at no further cost, but ensure that existing funds will be spent in a more “coherent and effective way”. Mróz-Gorgoń, meanwhile, noted that “the Poland brand is not the property of the government. It is created by entrepreneurs, artists, athletes, local governments and millions of Poles at home and abroad”. Developing this brand “means more investment, recognition of our brands and products abroad, and it also provides greater strength in international relations,” she continued. A suspected Russian Kh-101 cruise missile crashed in eastern Poland, around 100 km from the Ukrainian border, prompting the deployment of police counter-terrorism officers and other security services to the site. The fall of the object, which is reported to have caused a powerful explosion, left a crater about 10 metres wide and scattered fragments in a field between Tarnawa-Kolonia and Tokary in Lublin province, about 2 km from the nearest buildings, according to local police. World.title: Record number of Poles opposed to Ukraine’s EU membership
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Support for Ukraine joining the European Union has fallen sharply in Poland, with opposition reaching a record high of 40%, a survey carried out by the Polish state research agency CBOS shows. The figures show that 50% of Poles still support Ukraine’s EU membership, but that is a significant decline from 74% in October 2023, when the question was last asked, and from a record 90% in March 2022, shortly after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The shift comes as public sentiment towards Ukrainians in general in Poland has deteriorated in recent years. The latest CBOS poll shows that, among those who support Ukraine’s EU accession, most favour a gradual process, with 41% of all respondents saying Ukraine should join the EU but “without undue haste”. “Only 9% of respondents currently support Ukraine’s earliest possible EU membership, which is the lowest figure in the history of these surveys,” CBOS reported. Meanwhile, opposition to Ukraine’s EU membership has increased by 23 percentage points since October 2023, reaching its highest level in the history of CBOS surveys. People with right-wing political beliefs are most likely to be opposed to Ukraine’s accession (53%), while the age group with the highest percentage of people opposed is those aged 18-24 (58%). The survey also found that a majority of Poles expect the war in Ukraine to end with territorial concessions from Kyiv – 55% of respondents said they believed Ukraine would lose some territory, a view that has remained dominant since December 2024. Compared with the previous survey, however, pessimism has eased. The proportion of respondents who expect Ukraine to lose part of its territory fell by 8 percentage points, while the number expecting Russia to take control of the entire country declined from 8% to 6%. On Western support for Ukraine, 39% of respondents said the military, financial and humanitarian assistance provided by countries in the West was sufficient. Meanwhile, 27% said aid was excessive, while 22% said it was insufficient. Russia has published purported archival documents relating to massacres of Poles by Ukrainians in WWII. Kyiv had warned that Russia was planning to release the files in order to stir tensions, while Polish media note that the material contains nothing new https://t.co/CI0cfAlDle — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 6, 2026 Ukrainians are Poland’s largest foreign national group, with almost 1.6 million living in the country, but recent polls have shown growing hostility towards them, fuelled in part by anti-Ukrainian rhetoric from far-right parties and a tougher stance towards Kyiv from some opposition politicians. In its annual survey of attitudes towards national and ethnic groups, CBOS found earlier this year that the proportion of Poles who said they disliked Ukrainians increased by five percentage points this year, the largest rise recorded among all groups surveyed, reaching 43%. Tensions between the two countries have also been heightened by disputes over historical issues and a series of recent incidents targeting Ukrainians in Poland. The number of reported hate crimes against Ukrainians in Poland is up 30% so far this year, police data show. The figures come following recent high-profile cases of verbal and physical attacks against Ukrainians, who are Poland's largest immigrant group https://t.co/pcTsJddDz7 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 17, 2026 The number of reported hate crimes against Ukrainians rose by 30% in the first half of 2026 compared with the same period a year earlier, according to newly reported police data. Last weekend, three men were filmed violently attacking a Ukrainian woman and her partner outside a shop in Wrocław, apparently because of her accent. Two of the assailants have since been detained by police, while their victims required treatment in hospital. In response, Prime Minister Donald Tusk called for Poles to “wage war on violence”, saying that the perpetrators of such acts “have become emboldened precisely because they now have political role models, political patrons, and political support”. World.title: Newly sworn-in judge of Poland’s constitutional court stages boycott over blocked colleagues
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! A newly sworn-in judge of Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) has said he will refuse to sit on the court until four other judges appointed by parliament earlier this year, but blocked by the president, are allowed to take their seats. It is the latest development in a months-long dispute between the opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki and the government, which considers the TK to be improperly staffed and therefore illegitimate. Although Nawrocki swore in Sławomir Patyra, who was appointed by the ruling majority in parliament in June, as a TK judge on Tuesday, he continues to refuse to swear in four other judges appointed by parliament earlier this year. Po złożeniu przysięgi Patyra ogłosił, że zamierza odmówić orzekania. To gest solidarności z czwórką sędziów, od których prezydent nie chce przyjąć przysięgi https://t.co/jdbKusQ3H9 — OKO.press (@oko_press) July 28, 2026 Shortly after his swearing-in ceremony at the presidential palace on Tuesday, Patyra arrived at the TK headquarters in Warsaw, where he was accompanied by four other judges appointed by parliament this year, including two whom Nawrocki has refused to swear in. There, he announced that his decision not to sit on the court was a matter of loyalty to the constitution and his belief in judicial ethos. “I cannot imagine taking an oath today to uphold the constitution, only to start breaking that constitution tomorrow,” he said. Patyra told journalists that he would “submit a declaration of refusal to adjudicate” due to his solidarity with judges who are “unlawfully deprived of the chance to participate in the work of the tribunal”. He added that, along with the other judges chosen this year, he is “fully mobilised to restore the Constitutional Tribunal to its proper, constitutional, systemic form”. Under Polish law, when a vacancy emerges among the 15 positions on the TK, the lower house of parliament, the Sejm, chooses who should fill it. However, to take office, the judge must swear an oath before the president. In April, after the Sejm had chosen six candidates to fill vacancies on the court, Nawrocki took the unprecedented step of inviting only two of them to be sworn in. He argued there were doubts over the legality of how all six had been chosen, but decided to accept two to ensure the TK had the necessary quorum to function. Those two have been able to take up their seats on the court, but the other four remain in limbo. Although they arranged their own private swearing-in ceremony without the presence of Nawrocki, TK’s chief justice Bogdan Święczkowski has refused to accept them. In May, the European Court of Human Rights ordered that the quartet be allowed to take up their positions. But the TK – where judges appointed under the former Law and Justice (PiS) government retain a majority – issued its own ruling endorsing Nawrocki’s right not to swear in the new judges. The European Court of Human Rights has ordered Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) to accept four judges whom opposition-aligned President Nawrocki refused to swear in. The decision was welcomed by the government but rejected by the TK itself https://t.co/9NxInPdYk9 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 6, 2026 On 11 June, the Sejm then chose another judge, Patyra, to fill a newly opened vacancy on the court. In his case, the legal doubts Nawrocki had expressed regarding the previous appointments, which in some instances were made more than a year after the vacancies had arisen, did not seem to apply. Yet for weeks the president refused to confirm whether he would swear him in. That prompted Patyra to write to Nawrocki in early July and then again later in the month, asking the president to indicate a date on which he could take his oath. After repeated requests, Nawrocki finally decided last week to invite Patyra to the presidential palace. The president’s chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, noted that “there were some doubts” but “the president dispelled them” and added that Patyra was chosen “in accordance with all procedures”. Nowo wybrany przez Sejm Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej uchwałą z dnia 11 czerwca 2026 r. sędzia Trybunału Konstytucyjnego Sławomir Patyra złożył wobec Prezydenta RP ślubowanie. pic.twitter.com/VLMRAIg1Yj — Kancelaria Prezydenta RP (@prezydentpl) July 28, 2026 The TK has been at the heart of the rule-of-law crisis that has developed in Poland over the last decade. In 2015, former PiS-aligned President Andrzej Duda refused to swear in three judges legally chosen by the Sejm. Shortly afterwards, PiS won parliamentary elections and nominated three replacements for those judges, who were sworn in by Duda. Those three judges and their successors have been deemed illegitimate in a succession of rulings by Polish and European courts. Due to their continued presence on the court, the current government, which replaced PiS in 2023, rejects the TK’s legitimacy and refuses to recognise its rulings. Under both Święczkowski, a former member of the PiS government, and his predecessor Julia Przyłębska, a close personal associate of PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński, the TK has been widely seen as issuing rulings aligned with the political interests of PiS. Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Former Polish PM Morawiecki forms parliamentary caucus  rival to PiS, deepening opposition split
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Former Polish Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki says that 40 MPs and one senator aligned with him will form their own parliamentary group, deepening a split in the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) after a dispute over party direction and loyalty declarations. The move marks the most serious internal challenge in years to PiS, which ruled Poland from 2015 to 2023, and follows months of tensions between Morawiecki’s more moderate faction and party conservatives who have pushed the group in a hard-right direction. Once formally established, Morawiecki’s caucus would become the third-largest bloc in the Sejm, Poland’s lower house of parliament. Powstanie klub parlamentarny „Rozwój Plus”. Morawiecki zdecydował#PAPInformacjehttps://t.co/IftRdgpIPw — Polska Agencja Prasowa/Polish Press Agency (PAP) (@PAPinformacje) July 29, 2026 One of Morawiecki’s allies, Marcin Horała, told reporters that the creation of the caucus did not mean they were leaving PiS, but “simply setting up a parliamentary group so that we can get on with our work”. He noted, however, that PiS’s parliamentary group “has stopped treating us as its members”. Morawiecki, meanwhile, said that his group remained ready to cooperate with PiS as a “second lung” of the party’s broader political camp, but suggested that the group was moving in a different direction. He said that parts of PiS’s messaging were increasingly influenced by “dissidents and schemers” as well as hardline factions, including Sovereign Poland (Suwerenna Polska), a nationalist group that was previously a junior coalition partner of PiS and often clashed with Morawiecki when he was prime minister. Reacting to Morawiecki’s announcement, party chairman Jarosław Kaczyński said the former prime minister had carried out a planned split of the party despite his efforts to reach a deal. “Until the end I made efforts to reach an agreement, unfortunately Mateusz Morawiecki clearly had his own political plan in mind, carried out on the basis of a split in PiS,” Kaczyński wrote on X. The announcement follows a dispute that began after Morawiecki launched his Development Plus (Rozwój Plus) association in April. The former prime minister insisted the association was intended to complement PiS with a pro-development agenda rather than rival it. However, critics within PiS viewed it as an attempt by Morawiecki to build an alternative power base that could eventually evolve into a separate party ahead of the 2027 parliamentary election. Seeking to end the standoff, the party ordered PiS lawmakers to resign from all outside political associations by last Thursday, or face “consequences” including “the loss of membership in PiS”. On Friday, Kaczyński said that “around 30 MPs” had failed to comply and had therefore effectively resigned from the party, adding that Tuesday’s meeting of the party’s political committee would simply confirm this fact. Poland's right-wing opposition PiS party is set to split after a more moderate faction of over 30 MPs loyal to deputy leader @MorawieckiM refused to sign a loyalty pledge demanded by leader @OficjalnyJK, who says that means they have effectively resigned https://t.co/TuqYpGI5ak — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 24, 2026 On Tuesday, the party announced that instead, the committee had referred the cases of 44 members, who either failed to submit the required declarations or submitted them on the wrong form, to the party’s disciplinary officer for individual review, delaying a final decision. “From a formal and legal perspective, Mr Mateusz Morawiecki has not yet been removed from the list of members,” PiS spokesman Rafał Bochenek said on Tuesday. PiS disciplinary officer Karol Karski told the Polish Press Agency (PAP) he would examine each case individually. “I am open to speaking with each of them so they can present their positions,” Karski said. “At this point, I can initiate proceedings against the individual in question, refer the case to a peer disciplinary tribunal with a motion for punishment – this could include a temporary suspension or expulsion from PiS.” PiS has for the last two decades been the dominant force on the Polish right, including periods leading governments in 2005-2007 and 2015-2023. However, since losing power at elections in 2023, when the party won 35% of the vote, the party has seen its average support in polls fall to around 23-24%, the lowest level in 14 years. Support for PiS has fallen to its lowest in 14 years, as the party grapples with internal division, the rise of far-right challengers, living in President Nawrocki's shadow, and the unpopularity in Poland of PiS ally Donald Trump, writes @danieltilles1 https://t.co/QRScBpEQQG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 2, 2026 Meanwhile, it has been challenged by the rise of the far right, where two parties, Confederation (Konfederacja) and Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP), now together poll at a similar combined level of support to PiS. In response, Kaczyński in March named a hardline figure, Przemysław Czarnek, as PiS’s candidate for prime minister in next year’s elections. Czarnek was seen as someone who could appeal to far-right voters, while also potentially working with the far right if a coalition was needed after the elections. However, there has been no rise in support for PiS since Czarnek was named, prompting growing concern from more moderate figures within the party, led by Morawiecki. The national-conservative opposition PiS party has named its candidate to be prime minister if it wins next year’s parliamentary elections. Przemysław Czarnek is a hardline conservative who played a prominent role in PiS's campaign against "LGBT ideology" https://t.co/sSJLON00hW — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 7, 2026 They argue that PiS has wrongly disowned many of the successes of its time in office before 2023, and they fear that its rightward shift damages its chances of winning over more centrist voters. Adam Szłapka, the spokesman of the current more liberal government, said Braun was “the ultimate playmaker in this whole game”, who had helped push far-right rhetoric into the political mainstream. “The worst thing about this whole situation is that Poland’s largest opposition party has, in effect, started to adopt Grzegorz Braun’s agenda from A to Z,” Szłapka told broadcaster TVN24. Ostatecznym rozgrywającym w całej tej rozgrywce nie jest ani prezes Jarosław Kaczyński, ani Mateusz Morawiecki, tylko Grzegorz Braun – ocenił w #JedenNaJeden w TVN24 rzecznik rządu Adam Szłapka. W rozmowie z @AgataAdamek komentował sytuację w PiS. Czytaj więcej 💻⤵️… pic.twitter.com/TmJQk7izpG — tvn24 (@tvn24) July 29, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Polish court finds regulation allowing foreign same-sex marriage registration unconstitutional
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) has ruled that a new regulation allowing the registration of foreign same-sex marriage certificates in Poland was partly unconstitutional, saying it went beyond technical administrative changes and conflicted with the constitution’s definition of marriage. The regulation, introduced by the digital affairs ministry after rulings by the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) and Poland’s Supreme Administrative Court (NSA), was due to take effect on 23 August. The government, which considers the court to be improperly constituted, says it will not implement the ruling. The government has issued a regulation allowing foreign same-sex marriages to be entered in the civil registry The decision comes in response to an EU court order and marks a major change in a country that does not allow same-sex unions under domestic law https://t.co/2an5mGtnHl — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 22, 2026 Polish law does not allow same-sex couples to marry or enter into civil unions, and a bill that would have granted such limited rights to unmarried couples was recently vetoed by the opposition-backed president. Until this year, same-sex couples who married abroad were also unable to register their marriage certificates in Poland. After the CJEU ruled that Poland must recognise such marriages, the digital affairs ministry changed civil status forms. Instead of separate fields for “man” and “woman”, the new templates use “man/woman”, allowing registry offices to record both opposite-sex and same-sex marriages. Lawmakers from the national-conservative opposition Law and Justice (PiS) party, however, challenged the regulation, arguing that the digital affairs minister had exceeded his powers because the changes were not merely technical but affected the legal definition of marriage. The tribunal, which is widely seen as being under PiS’s influence, agreed. The tribunal said the new forms allowed relationships that do not match the constitution’s definition of marriage as a union between a man and a woman to be recorded as marriages. It said regulations can only implement existing laws and cannot change matters reserved for the constitution or parliament. The tribunal also said that registering a foreign marriage certificate cannot produce legal effects that conflict with the basic principles of Polish law. It added that changing the constitutional definition of marriage would require amendments to the constitution and related laws. Some legal experts argue that, while the constitution states that a “marriage, being a union of a man and a woman… shall be placed under the protection and care of the Republic of Poland,” that phrasing does not rule out other legally recognised unions receiving state protection. Poland has begun recognising foreign same-sex marriages. But the legal consequences for such couples remain unclear, especially as Polish law does not allow any form of same-sex union We asked five experts for their view on what this will mean in practice https://t.co/h2KHmW8sMI — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 19, 2026 Shortly after the ruling, government members said they would not comply with the tribunal’s decision and that the regulation would enter into force as planned. “The illegal Constitutional Tribunal is once again attempting to obstruct a state that is enforcing the law in force and the rulings of European courts,” digital affairs minister Krzysztof Gawkowski said. “The transcription of foreign same-sex marriage certificates is and will remain legal,” he said, adding that 184 same-sex couples had so far had their foreign marriage certificates transcribed. Katarzyna Kotula, the government official responsible for equality issues, said the TK ruling on the issue of transcriptions “has no legal force whatsoever”. Nielegalny Trybunał Konstytucyjny po raz kolejny próbuje zatrzymać państwo, które wykonuje obowiązujące prawo i wyroki europejskich sądów. Transkrypcja zagranicznych aktów małżeństw jednopłciowych jest i będzie legalna. Rozporządzenie, które przyjęliśmy porządkuje dokumenty i… — Krzysztof Gawkowski (@KGawkowski) July 28, 2026 The TK has been at the heart of the rule-of-law crisis that has developed in Poland over the last decade. In 2015, former PiS-aligned President Andrzej Duda refused to swear in three judges legally chosen by the Sejm. Shortly afterwards, PiS won parliamentary elections and nominated three replacements for those judges, who were sworn in by Duda. Those three judges and their successors have been deemed illegitimate in a succession of rulings by Polish and European courts. Due to their continued presence on the court, the current government, which replaced PiS in 2023, rejects the TK’s legitimacy and refuses to recognise its rulings. Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 Under both Święczkowski, a former member of the PiS government, and his predecessor Julia Przyłębska, a close personal associate of PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński, the TK has been widely seen as issuing rulings aligned with the political interests of PiS. For a long time, the government refused to appoint new judges to the Constitutional Tribunal as the terms of the previous judges expired, with some vacancies remaining unfilled for over a year. In recent months, the government has resumed appointing new judges, but President Karol Nawrocki, an ally of PiS, is refusing to administer the oath of office to some of them.
